This fund backs projects strengthening human resilience across three pillars—life, space, and community—supporting founders who rebuild not just businesses, but themselves, and in doing so redefine how the world is built.

funds.name: Freedom of Art Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting artists who honor cultural lineage, uplift community, and push creative expression forward through music, storytelling, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
funds.description: The Freedom of Art Fund invests in creators who treat art as legacy, service, and evolution. Rooted in the cultural lineage of jazz and Black American music, this fund supports musicians, storytellers, educators, and interdisciplinary artists creating work that heals, connects, and empowers communities across generations and geographies. From recordings and performances to education, multimedia, and community-based initiatives, Freedom of Art champions integrity, collaboration, and artistic excellence as tools for collective growth.

funds.name: FTC Fund for Public Goods
funds.subtitle: Digital public infrastructure to steward and protect the commons as AI concentrates power
funds.description:
AI is generating enormous economic surplus, and left alone, both the surplus and the control over it concentrate in a few hands. Funding the Commons Frontier Fund backs the people building the alternative: funding, governance, and coordination systems that communities, institutions, and autonomous agents can use in the open, that stay auditable and forkable, and that no single company or state can quietly switch off.
This season we're concentrating on the AI-native layer of that work. Programmable funding and treasury systems, coordination and payment infrastructure for autonomous agents, governance that constrains those agents transparently, sovereign and open-source AI, and tools that keep communities in control of their own data and compute. Funding, governance, and coordination mechanisms more broadly are still welcome.
We fund things that are deployed and making impact in the wild. Some projects within this fund have been incubated by Funding the Commons, through our residencies, hackathons, and other activities. Projects may be invited to go on to work with Commons Lab, the new for-profit for-purpose incubator of Funding the Commons, for hands-on support and introductions to institutions that can deploy their work. We back the work in public and publish what holds and what breaks, so the field can build on it.

funds.name: Fula Fund for Empowering the Future of Web3 Storage
funds.subtitle: Seeking visionary creators building on decentralized data solutions.
funds.description:
The Fula Fund is a catalyst for innovative projects building on the Fula Network, a decentralized storage solution designed for creators and applications. We're seeking pioneers who share our vision of a future where data is freely accessible, securely stored, and cost-effective. Whether you're crafting stunning NFTs, building the next-gen metaverse platform, or developing a revolutionary streaming service, the Fula Match Fund can fuel your ambitions.
Benefits:
Matching Funds: The Fula Fund provides financial support to help propel your project forward. We'll match your fundraising efforts, up to a certain amount, to accelerate your development and growth.
Free Fula Storage: Unleash the power of decentralized storage! Fula Fund recipients receive free storage on the Fula Network, allowing you to focus on building without worrying about storage costs.
Exposure & Support: Gain valuable exposure to the Fula community and the wider Web3 ecosystem. We'll promote your project through our channels and connect you with potential collaborators and investors.
The Fula Fund is more than just funding. It's a call to action for visionaries who share our passion for a decentralized future. Are you ready to build on the Fula Network and shape the future of Web3 storage? Submit your application today!

funds.name: Fund of Infinite Yes
funds.subtitle: Funding radical storytellers building the next generation of empathy machines—cinematic and immersive experiences that collapse distance and reconnect humanity.
funds.description:
We are living in an age of infinite scroll—private screens glowing in dark rooms, each of us alone inside personalized feeds. Shared experience has fractured into isolated consumption. And yet the motion picture remains the most powerful empathy technology ever invented, changing how we see one another—and ourselves.
The Fund of Infinite Yes Fund exists to push that technology forward.
We support visionary creators who treat cinema and immersive media not as content, but as infrastructure for human connection. These are works that dissolve the frame, collapse distance, and transform passive spectators into participants—projects that challenge, provoke, and deepen our emotional bandwidth. Projects that reject numb algorithmic spectacle and instead build spaces—physical and virtual—where we feel with each other again.
Beneath the scroll is communion. The future of media will not be flatter or faster. It will be more immersive, more collective, more human.
An infinite yes to the machines that make us more alive.

funds.name: Future Aesthetics Fund for Worlds Worth Building
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists, writers, designers, architects, and scientists creating optimistic, realistic visions of the future.
funds.description:
The Future Aesthetics Fund supports artists and scientists who imagine new worlds worth building. We believe the stories, images, discoveries, and ideas a civilization shares about tomorrow shape what it chooses to discover and build today. Run by the Foundation for Future Aesthetics, a nonprofit advancing optimistic, realistic visions of the future through art, science, and culture, this fund champions speculative fiction, visual art, design, architecture, exhibitions, and interdisciplinary projects that replace dystopian sentiment with ambitious, achievable futures that we can adopt and act to bring about.
Note for applying projects:
Our curators assess project submissions on a rolling basis, and will make a determination about your project submission by or on the nearest Sunday. Thanks for your patience!

funds.name: FWB Fund for Builders
funds.subtitle: Bridging the Gap Between Technical Innovation and Cultural Relevance
funds.description: Technical innovation in web3 is accelerating, but without cultural relevance, even the most powerful tools struggle to achieve meaningful adoption. The FWB Fund for Builders supports a new wave of Creative Technologists—builders who merge technical expertise with cultural fluency. This fund backs projects that integrate emergent technologies, such as AI Agents, into web3 in ways that drive real-world impact and sustainable adoption.

funds.name: Get Set UP (with Funds)
funds.subtitle: Empowering street artists to reclaim public space and foster authentic community through live painting.
funds.description: The UP Fund champions the raw brilliance of street art, graffiti, and urban expression. As an NYC-based publication rooted in the pulse of the city, UP supports artists who paint in public, outside of institutions, and often against the odds. This Fund is dedicated to projects that bring live painting to the streets, showcase emerging voices, and celebrate the vibrancy of urban culture while fostering true community connection.

funds.name: GLITCH Fund for Arts & Tech
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists and engineers pushing the boundaries of creative expression through digital art, blockchain, AI, and emerging technologies.
funds.description: The GLITCH Fund supports visionary creators working at the intersection of art, technology, and societal transformation. We believe the most exciting breakthroughs emerge when artists, engineers, researchers, and builders collaborate across disciplines. From blockchain-native artworks and AI experiments to open-source creative tools and new cultural protocols, this fund celebrates projects that challenge conventions, embrace experimentation, and expand the frontier of what art can become. Inspired by six years of residencies, exhibitions, and collective creation, GLITCH champions openness, collaboration, and technological innovation as pathways to artistic exploration.

funds.name: Global Music Fund
funds.subtitle: Fueling cross-cultural collaboration through music that bridges borders, languages, genres, and generations.
funds.description: The Global Music Fund supports visionary creators building bold, collaborative music projects that span continents, languages, and genres. We invest in artists using music as a tool to dissolve boundaries, uplift underrepresented voices, and foster global understanding. Whether through tracks, tech, or transformative experiences, this fund backs projects that unite diverse musicians to shape a more inclusive, interconnected world.

funds.name: Gonzo Sovereign Press Fund
funds.subtitle: Seeking fearless journalists, documentarians, and storytellers creating permanent records that power cannot erase.
funds.description: The Gonzo Sovereign Press Fund supports independent journalists who immerse themselves in the story, challenge powerful institutions, and publish work that deserves to endure. We believe journalism should be owned by its creators—not platforms—and remain permanently accessible to the public. From investigative reporting and gonzo journalism to documentary films, podcasts, and narrative nonfiction, we champion storytellers creating lasting records that deepen public understanding and strengthen a free press.

funds.name: Gray Area Fund for Cultural Innovation
funds.subtitle: Fueling breakthrough in art and technology that reimagine culture and empower community.
funds.description: The Gray Area Fund supports creators working across art, technology, science, and the humanities to build more equitable and regenerative futures. We champion bold experimentation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and projects that push the boundaries of cultural expression while engaging communities through meaningful, impactful experiences.

funds.name: Greenpill Fund for Regenerative Gatherings
funds.subtitle: Supporting local events from active greenpill chapters and potential stewards to learn, build, and take root.
funds.description:
In season 6, The Greenpill Fund for Regenerative Gatherings backs in-person events that strengthen the bonds of regenerative communities. Whether it’s a workshop, meetup, or cultural celebration with over 30 different projects.
In season 7, Greenpill Network will focus on existing Greenpill Chapters and onboarding potential stewards to Greenpill Network, which are deepen local roots, and turn regenerative ideals into real-world impact.

funds.name: Habitat Fund for Wild Realities
funds.subtitle: Supporting immersive experiences that reshape how humans relate to nature and help catalyze regenerative futures.
funds.description: The Habitat Fund for Wild Realities supports creators using immersive and experiential media to repair the human–nature relationship. Launched in partnership with the Habitat Nature Parks Foundation, an organization at the forefront of immersive nature storytelling, this fund champions powerful experiences—virtual, physical, and hybrid—that can shift perception, influence systems, and inspire long-term stewardship. We back projects that move beyond awareness toward meaningful ecological and cultural impact, pairing funding with mentorship and curatorial support to help ambitious ideas grow into real-world change.

funds.name: Harmonia Fund for Women in Art & Tech for Environmental Furtherance
funds.subtitle: Empowering women creators who through art & tech drive ecological furtherance
funds.description: The Guardians of Gaia Fund supports women-led projects at the vanguard of cultural+environmental transformation—visionary creators weaving together regenerative design, emerging technologies, and ancestral wisdom. We champion those crafting new myths, healing modalities, and collaborative systems that seed a more conscious, equitable, and thriving planet.

funds.name: Haus of Us Fund for Queer Creators
funds.subtitle: Supporting LGBTQ+ creators building culture, community and new futures through art and media—on our terms.
funds.description: The Haus of Us Fund exists to resource LGBTQ+ creators who are expanding culture, imagination, and collective understanding, often without access to traditional funding or institutional support. Rooted in chosen family, shared stewardship, and non-extractive care, this fund treats queer creativity as a living 'queer creative commons,' a shared cultural ecosystem shaped by artists, storytellers, and makers across entertainment, art and media. We support work that strengthens this commons through integrity, cultural relevance, and community responsibility rather than credentials or hype.

funds.name: HERDAO Fund for Emerging Kenyan Builders
funds.subtitle: For Emerging African Builders supports early stage  projects
funds.description: The H.E.R. DAO Fund for Emerging African Builders supports early-stage creators in Africa who are building tech and Web3 projects despite limited access to capital. Rooted in H.E.R. DAO’s mission to make technology more inclusive, this fund champions young developers, designers, and digital creators with demonstrated momentum. We prioritize projects that show real progress, creative ambition, and the potential to create meaningful economic or community impact, helping Africa’s next generation of builders take their work to the next level.

funds.name: Hispanic Impact Fund
funds.subtitle: Empowering Hispanic communities in Central Texas by supporting innovative projects in early childhood education, health and wellness, job skills and entrepreneurship, and leadership development.
funds.description: The Hispanic Impact Fund champions the economic mobility of Hispanic Central Texans by supporting visionary projects that align with our four key impact areas. With a commitment to equity and community-driven decision-making, we prioritize initiatives led by and for Hispanic communities, ensuring sustainable change and measurable impact. Whether fostering early learning, advancing health, building career pathways, or nurturing leadership, this fund uplifts organizations making a tangible difference.

funds.name: Hope Fund for Collective Futures
funds.subtitle: Backing creative works that help people imagine a better future and feel their own agency in creating it
funds.description:
Hope does not mean pretending that things are fine. It means looking honestly at what is broken, while refusing to surrender the possibility of repair. Hope is not only a feeling, but a practical and imaginative capacity: the ability to see meaningful goals, discover pathways toward them, and feel enough agency to begin moving.
Despair is free; every headline delivers it. Hope takes craft. This fund backs the creators who practice that craft: creative works and participatory experiences whose explicit goal is to raise hope, helping people imagine a better future and feel empowered to create it.

funds.name: Hubs Network Fund for Commons Residencies
funds.subtitle: We connect physical spaces and (tech) talent for local, mission-driven residencies at Hubs in the PULSIN Network..
funds.description: Independent physical spaces, ecovillages, hacker spaces, community hubs, generate enormous value that mostly goes unfunded and uncounted. This fund resources the Hubs & Pilgrims model: hubs turn real local challenges into scoped residency projects with clear objectives, and traveling pilgrims with the right skills come to execute them, hosted and fed by the space they serve. Instead of vague volunteering, every residency is a defined project with measurable goals and documented outcomes, making the invisible value of the commons tangible while demonstrating another way of living and working together.

funds.name: Hubs Network Fund for Solarpunk Spaces
funds.subtitle: Seeking independent physical spaces building new models for culture, care, governance, and the commons.
funds.description: The Hubs Network Fund supports independent physical spaces where people practice new forms of collaboration, governance, culture, technology, and care in real life. From makerspaces and hackerspaces to colivings, intentional communities, counterculture spaces, and artist collectives, we believe these hubs are society’s R&D layer—fragile, vital, and too often underfunded.

funds.name: Human Bloom Collective Fund
funds.subtitle: A learning engine for human flourishing, funding creators who make possible futures tangible.
funds.description: How do we increase human capacity, agency, connection, creativity, resilience, access, and trust as technology and society evolve? Human Bloom Collective Fund turns that question outward, supporting interdisciplinary creators, artists, designers, technologists, scientists, game makers, and community builders, who make important possibilities real enough to encounter, test, learn from, and share. Its breadth is deliberate: the most consequential questions about flourishing now live between fields, between technology and nature, digital and physical life, innovation and tradition, and this fund gives those intersections a place to become work.

funds.name: Humanitarian Fund for Displaced Storytellers
funds.subtitle: Revolutionize refugee aid by leveraging blockchain technology to create new mechanisms for the preservation of cultural heritage.
funds.description: The Humanitarian Fund is a beacon of hope, leveraging blockchain technology to not only provide immediate support to refugees but also to capture and preserve the rich cultural tapestry that defines their identity. Through multimedia storytelling—including videos, audio recordings, art, interviews, music videos, books, essays, photo essays, and photojournalism—we aim to capture the essence of refugee experiences. This fund places a paramount importance on safeguarding oral histories and cultural traditions, particularly those conveyed by oral historians within refugee communities who may lack literacy in English or any written language. By preserving these narratives through recorded interviews and subsequent translations, we ensure that these precious forms of cultural knowledge, which are at risk of being lost forever, are instead made immutable and censorship-resistant on the blockchain.

funds.name: HyperDeSci fund for Open Science
funds.subtitle: Fueling decentralized science through open research and collaboration.
funds.description:
✨ The HyperDeSci Fund supports scientists and collectives in their early-stage transition to Web3, pioneering decentralized, open science.
✨ We champion projects that expand public knowledge, based on the scientific method, enhance collaboration, and commit to open-source transparency.
✨ By backing these efforts at their inception, we catalyze a thriving DeSci ecosystem rooted in merit, community, and curiosity.
Website
Whitepaper
✨ SPONSOR AIRDROP: Upon completion of the season, all sponsors will receive HyperDeSci governance tokens proportional to their contribution, as well as immediately tradable $FURMION memecoin rewards.
✨ Join our Telegram chat for updates and inquiries.

funds.name: Ikigai Fund for Creative Purpose
funds.subtitle: Seeking creators at the very beginning of a new chapter, ready to explore where their passion, their talent, and what the world needs finally meet.
funds.description: The Ikigai Fund supports creators in the earliest, most tender stage of their work: the moment when a project is still forming and a person is still discovering what they are truly called to make. Ikigai is the Japanese idea of a life well aimed, the intersection of what you love, what you are good at, what the world needs, and what can sustain you. Fund director Paige Donner knows the territory firsthand: in 2018 she walked away from her role as a Paris lifestyle editor for USA Today to build a company in emerging technology, and she has spent years since helping founders and creators navigate their own pivots toward more aligned work. This fund extends that mission with microgrants for people in career transition who want to express themselves through art, science, literature, or music, giving them just enough breathing room to create from curiosity instead of financial stress. Funded creators join a cohort that builds trust together, including through The Ikigai Game, with in-person gatherings on the horizon, because finding your purpose is easier in good company.

funds.name: Illuminate Fund for Citizen Scientists
funds.subtitle: Empowering the next generation of citizen scientists through education, technology, and public engagement.
funds.description: Illuminate supports non-commercial and open-source projects that bridge the gap between public understanding and the frontier of science and technology. We foster innovative partnerships between researchers, artists, educators, and engineers in order to democratize science and make vital functional literacy skills more accessible. We fund the development of engaging classroom tools, interactive platforms, and science education initiatives—from generative art exploring quantum computing to social networks for citizen scientists documenting research fraud. Illuminate empowers creators who make complex topics meaningful and who equip learners of all ages and backgrounds with the actionable skills needed to thrive in a knowledge-driven future.

funds.name: Immersive Bliss Fund for VR Films
funds.subtitle: Supporting visionary creators producing premium 180° stereoscopic films for Apple Vision Pro, setting new standards in immersive storytelling.
funds.description: Immersive Bliss is on a mission to elevate immersive entertainment by curating and distributing top-tier 180° stereoscopic films for Apple Vision Pro. This match fund champions high-quality, short-form experiences—whether pre-rendered or live-action—that push the boundaries of storytelling in spatial cinema. Selected projects will be featured on the Immersive Bliss platform, connecting creators with a growing audience eager for cutting-edge immersive content.

funds.name: Impossible Arts Fund for Generative Cinema
funds.subtitle: Supporting fiercely independent filmmakers using generative AI to create original, emotionally powerful narrative films that could not exist through traditional cinema.
funds.description: The Impossible Arts Fund for Generative Cinema champions a new class of filmmakers proving that generative AI can produce true cinematic art. We support bold, narrative-driven short films that are emotionally resonant, philosophically ambitious, and formally daring—projects once deemed impossible due to cost, scale, or industry gatekeeping. This fund exists to replace tech demos with undeniable cinema and to help visionary outsiders make films whose power comes because of generative tools, not in spite of them.

funds.name: Indigenous XR Fund
funds.subtitle: For emerging or experienced Indigenous artists/creators in XR technology.
funds.description: The Indigenous XR Fund supports visionary Indigenous artists, storytellers, and technologists who harness (or would like to harness) AR and VR to reclaim culture, revitalize language, and craft immersive experiences rooted in ancestral knowledge. We believe Native Futurists are not only preserving heritage—they are reimagining tomorrow.

funds.name: Innovation Fund for Adobe Creators
funds.subtitle: Empowering creators who push the boundaries of storytelling with Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, and cutting-edge AI tools.
funds.description: The Innovation Fund champions visionary filmmakers and creators leveraging Adobe’s latest technology—AI-driven scene editing, automated rotoscoping, real-time collaboration, and seamless Creative Cloud integration—to craft groundbreaking narratives. Whether you’re producing indie documentaries or immersive VFX-driven shorts, this fund supports those who transform ideas into compelling cinematic experiences through technical excellence and creative innovation.

funds.name: INTERSECTIONS Fund for Techno-Artists
funds.subtitle: Fueling the next generation of builders who merge machine learning with multimedia expression.
funds.description: The INTERSECTIONS Fund backs self-taught builders, curious students, and experimental technologists at the edges of machine learning, art, and science. We support creators who turn data into poetry, algorithms into art, and interfaces into immersive storytelling. From BCI-powered installations to generative games built on web archives, this Fund celebrates those who craft meaningful, multisensory experiences that challenge how we engage with technology—and with each other.

funds.name: Ipê Fund for Internet-Native Institutions
funds.subtitle: Supporting builders and creators making tools, prototypes, gatherings, and media that turn internet-native communities into working institutions.
funds.description: Ipê City has spent three years prototyping new ways to live together: month-long pop-up villages, hacker houses, residencies, grants, and a documentary series about people building new societies around the world. We believe the systems that run our lives, from governance and education to healthcare and identity, deserve a rebuild on the technologies of this century, mainly AI and open blockchains. This fund backs builders, organizers, and creators with working prototypes, active projects, events, or clear creative output, whether that is coordination software, a community experiment, or art and gatherings that spread techno-optimistic culture. Funded projects join a network of Ipê Architects who ship in public, share what they learn, and help every experiment make the next one more durable.

funds.name: Isla Impact Fund
funds.subtitle: Backing new earth projects on Ibiza: art, regeneration, education, and community on one island small enough to change whole.
funds.description: Ibiza is known to the world for its nights. Look closer and you find something else growing: farms returning to life, cooperatively owned spaces taking shape, artists and stewards choosing the island as home ground for a different way of living. This fund backs that quieter Ibiza. It supports musicians, visual artists, performers, and filmmakers rooted in the island; builders of alternative and experiential learning; conservationists rewilding land and sea; researchers studying regeneration and consciousness; designers of circular materials and community-owned spaces; cooperatives and collective-ownership ventures; and the ceremonial and healing practitioners who hold the culture together. An island is a whole world at a scale where care is visible. What proves true on Ibiza can travel anywhere.

funds.name: JOY Fund for Healing Arts
funds.subtitle: Supporting healing artists, somatic practitioners, and community care workers building accessible, decolonized wellness spaces around the world.
funds.description: Born in Berlin and reaching worldwide, the JOY Fund backs the people already doing the work of care: sound healers, breathwork facilitators, somatic practitioners, therapists, and community organizers creating trauma-informed spaces where healing is accessible, culturally grounded, and led by community rather than industry. The fund grows from JOY Collective, a Berlin healing collective of 50+ practitioners whose work spans free community support circles, ancestral and indigenous healing traditions, and land-based retreat spaces from Senegal to the Philippines, all guided by one conviction: wellness should be decolonized, rooted in dignity, and within everyone's reach.

funds.name: Juicebox Project Accelerator Fund
funds.subtitle: Seeking community-driven projects from the creators of tomorrow.
funds.description: The Juicebox Project Accelerator Fund is a catalyst for community-driven projects from the creators of tomorrow. We support projects that push the boundaries of innovation and that are deeply rooted in community governance and ownership. This fund champions projects that launch on Juicebox, a programmable fundraising platform, aligning with our mission to connect millions of creators and contributors in the most transparent and community-oriented way.

funds.name: Junglepunk Fund for Intergenerational Agriculture
funds.subtitle: Funding junglepunk stewards growing food forests, seed lineages, and intergenerational resilience for the network societ
funds.description: This fund backs the people growing the future from the ground up: food foresters, seed stewards, and community cultivators restoring abundance through living systems. Run by AgroforestDAO and rooted in syntropic agroforestry, ancestral memory, and cyber-coordination, it supports projects building a rooted network society shaped by seasonal rhythms, intergenerational wealth, and cyberstigmergy

funds.name: Kindhearted Fund for Artists Who Give Back
funds.subtitle: For those who give back: funding creators whose track record of community impact reaches beyond their art
funds.description:
Some artists nourish their communities twice. Once through the work itself, and again through everything around it: free music lessons for young people, workshops that open doors, community tun production companies, infrastructure that promises a more just future for the next generation.
Kindhearted Artists Impact Fund backs artists with a demonstrated record of exactly that kind of impact: creators who change how people see things or how people do things, and who spend their own time and resources lifting up others. Think of filmmakers who runs visual storytelling workshops while producing their friends' films, DJs who develop open source platforms, or established musicians in London and Ramallah who build community hubs and teach young people to play for free because they believe in opening doors.
Every applicant submits an impact strategy, and the fund gives strong preference to practices connected to peacemaking, justice, rematriation, and anti-patriarchal and anti-colonial approaches. The goal is simple: put resources behind the artists who have already proven they multiply whatever they are given.

funds.name: Kuzana Experiments Fund
funds.subtitle: Backing radically better ways to build wealth in Kenya & Kuzana ecosystem
funds.description: Africa has plenty of capital for ideas that already fit into a box: the venture-backed startup, the NGO project, the research grant, the government program. This fund is interested in what happens before the box exists. A community of floating homes that rearrange themselves on Kilifi Creek. A wellbeing platform that folds movement, book clubs, and discussion groups into the working week. A public rating system that lets entrepreneurs see how funders actually behave. A community-owned business, a new way to finance small firms, a governance experiment that sounds slightly crazy until somebody tries it. Kuzana is a made-up word that sounds, in Swahili, like helping each other grow, and that is the method here: small, concrete tests run by builders in Kenya who are close enough to meet, sharpen each other, and share what worked and what failed. Some experiments will fail. Good. The goal is not to predict the future correctly; it is to make enough intelligent attempts that we discover the pieces of the future worth scaling.

funds.name: LAB Open Source Builders Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting African developers building open-source Bitcoin infrastructure, financial tools, and decentralized systems for the next generation of the digital economy.
funds.description:
The LAB Open Source Builders Fund supports African developers building open-source infrastructure across the Bitcoin ecosystem, with a primary focus on empowering African builders.
Created by Let Africa Build (LAB), this fund empowers emerging developers to experiment, prototype, and launch tools that strengthen decentralized finance, payment systems, and developer infrastructure across Africa. By supporting early-stage experimentation, the fund helps transform promising developers into startup founders and contributors to the global Bitcoin ecosystem.

funds.name: LATAM Fund for Creative Communities
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists, cultural workers, and community builders strengthening creative ecosystems across Latin America.
funds.description: The LATAM Fund for Creative Communities supports artists, cultural workers, technologists, and organizers building the future of creativity across Latin America. From visual arts and music to cultural production, community initiatives, and emerging technologies, we champion projects that strengthen local creative ecosystems, celebrate cultural identity, and foster collaboration across the region. Our mission is to empower the creators and community builders whose work enriches culture, expands opportunity, and connects people through shared creative experiences.

funds.name: Lattice Fund for Living Worlds
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists and creative technologists who turn physical movement into living virtual worlds using sensors, open-source tools, and a regenerative spirit.
funds.description: The Lattice Fund for Living Worlds supports interactive art that listens to the physical world. Using simple sensors, projects translate movement, footsteps across a room, wind through leaves, a crowd at a festival, into data that grows evolving virtual worlds. The fund grew out of Lattice, an open-source framework built by young South African developers from Younglings Africa, whose first installation let an audience unknowingly grow a digital ecosystem just by moving through the space. We champion projects that close the loop between the world you grow and the ground it came from: regeneration, recycling, habitat, community.

funds.name: Learning Layer Fund for AI Frontiers
funds.subtitle: Supporting creators building art, science, and technology projects at the frontier of artificial intelligence.
funds.description: The Learning Layer Fund supports creators exploring the rapidly evolving frontier of artificial intelligence. Powered by the community around Learning Layer Labs at Frontier Tower in San Francisco, this fund backs artists, engineers, researchers, and builders experimenting with new forms of AI-native creativity and technology. From agent-based systems and vibe-coded software to immersive installations and research explorations, we champion projects that push the boundaries of what becomes possible when humans collaborate with intelligent machines.

funds.name: Leverage Fund for Revolutionary Science
funds.subtitle: Seeking scrappy scientific teams pursuing revolutionary breakthroughs through bold theories, decisive experiments, and new scientific instruments.
funds.description: The Leverage Fund for Revolutionary Science supports revolutionary research in fields at the cutting edge of human knowledge. We believe the next scientific revolution will emerge not from established labs, but from exceptional individuals and teams working in new and emerging fields. Projects that offer prizes or support to specific revolutionary science efforts are also welcome.

funds.name: Living Lab Kesennuma Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding builders who test AI, blockchain, and emerging tech against the real challenges of a Japanese coastal city.
funds.description: Kesennuma, a fishing city in northeastern Japan, has opened itself as a living laboratory for emerging technology and social challenge. This fund backs developers, researchers, and technologists from Japan and abroad who build AI, blockchain, and emerging-tech solutions for the realities of a shrinking regional city: fisheries data and traceability, local economic circulation, and sustained engagement between newcomers and the region. Many are early-career engineers applying their skills to a real municipality for the first time, with city staff, fishery workers, and residents as their collaborators and their judges.

funds.name: Living Presence Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding creators who deepen human presence through shared, embodied experience.
funds.description: In an increasingly digital world, the rarest luxury is genuine human presence: a shared table, live music, storytelling around a fire, silence held together in nature. Living Presence Fund supports artists, musicians, chefs, filmmakers, storytellers, and facilitators whose work brings people into direct experience with one another, work that cannot be measured by algorithms or audience size. It invests in depth over visibility, backing practitioners of exceptional craft and the interdisciplinary collaborations that none of them could create alone.

funds.name: Living Water Legacy Fund
funds.subtitle: Remembering We are All Water - teaching w/ community-led regenerative storytelling, watershed restoration & agriculture.
funds.description:
Water is the Source of Life and Water is our common bond with All Life. Yet we humans have forgotten this truth. We are living through a strange species-wide amnesia—we have forgotten how to celebrate, honor and cherish that which gives us our existence.
The Living Water Legacy Fund is formed to help us remember this: We are all in this game together. By backing, co-creating, and implementing community-led projects that restore remembrance and connection to our ourselves, each other, AND our watershed biomes, we strive generate the kinds of actions that will bring us hydrological, ecological and social balance—on behalf of present and future generation of All Life.
The projects we are looking to support might include an artist creating an immersive art piece or group of musician composing a song sing their love of Water; a community cooperative ensuring access to secure clean water and food sovereignty; piece of software encouraging regenerative agriculture; or community establishing an archive for preserving their ancestral ecological knowledge before it disappears.
We are emphasizing collaborative efforts: from the restoration of a 15-acre regeneration farm near the source of the Nile in Uganda to youth media studios inside Watershed Community Revitalization Centers throughout Guinea, West Africa; from the return of an ancient Water ceremony from the Indigenous People of Colombia to a simple video series sharing Water's beauty—the possibilities are endless.
The fund is hosted by the WaterUnity Networks and a cohort of Water-loving curators led by Eliza Herald, who has spent over 33 years crafting stories and strategies that move humanity toward caring for our Water, land, and community resilience. We are guided by a simple principle: We are all Water, and those communities living closest to the Water and the land it nurtures must be empowered to shape the decisions that affect our lives.

funds.name: Lovepunks Fund for Experiential Culture
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists, musicians, builders, and community creators co-designing new cultural experiences, rituals, and spaces for human connection.
funds.description: The Lovepunks Fund for Experiential Culture supports artists, musicians, researchers, designers, organizers, technologists, and social innovators creating human-centered experiences that bring people together. From music residencies and cultural laboratories to rituals, gatherings, pop-up communities, and creative experiments, we fund projects that explore new ways of connecting, creating, learning, and living together. Our mission is to cultivate cultural infrastructure that strengthens human relationships, nurtures creativity, and leaves behind lasting contributions that can inspire communities around the world.

funds.name: Magical Technologies Fund for Personal Transformation
funds.subtitle: For founders building research-grounded tools that make self-understanding feel like magic.
funds.description: The best technology has always felt like magic: it produces a shift in the person experiencing it before they can explain how. This fund supports founders building tools for a healthier society, work grounded in research and designed to deliver genuinely transformative experience, with a focus on better understanding of the self as part of a collective of high-agency individuals.

funds.name: MAIX Fund for LATAM XR Creators
funds.subtitle: Empowering independent XR creators across Latin America to tell stories that matter through innovative and ethical immer
funds.description:
The MAIX Fund supports Latin American XR artists creating powerful, cross-disciplinary work that speaks to the region’s complex cultural and social realities. By uplifting hybrid narratives rooted in popular culture, identity, and ethical practice, the fund aims to ignite a new wave of immersive storytelling that is as technically bold as it is socially resonant.
Winners will participate in Festivals like Curta Brasilia (Brazil), VRFest and GIFF (Mexico), #NarrarElFuturo (Colombia), and more. They will also receive three hours of consulting from community experts.
Learn more at maix.art

funds.name: Making + Thinking Fund
funds.subtitle: Fueling interdisciplinary projects that reimagine the intersections of art, thought, and social transformation.
funds.description: The Making + Thinking Fund supports artists, researchers, and activists challenging disciplinary norms to build a just and sustainable world. We back bold experiments in art and pedagogy that question convention and embody radical imagination. If your work lives at the intersection of making and thinking, this fund is for you.

funds.name: Manantial Blanco LATAM Digital Art Fund
funds.subtitle: Amplifying Latin American voices through digital art, music, and creative storytelling.
funds.description:
The Manantial Blanco LATAM Digital Art Fund champions human-made creations from Latin American artists who infuse soul, story, and texture into their digital work. Drawing inspiration from rich folk traditions such as alebrijes, this fund celebrates artwork where the artist's distinctive touch remains visible—where imperfections become beauty and technique itself tells a story. Artists are encouraged to explore the mythic world of the Alebrijes Universe and, for those interested, official Alebrijes® and Calaveras Linares® IP is available for incorporation into their creative projects.
El Premio de Arte Digital Latinoamericano de Manantial Blanco impulsa creaciones hechas por artistas Latinoamericanos que infunden alma, narrativa y textura en su trabajo digital. Inspirándose en ricas tradiciones folclóricas como los Alebrijes, este fondo celebra obras donde el toque distintivo del artista permanece visible—donde las imperfecciones se convierten en belleza y la técnica misma cuenta una historia. Se anima a los artistas a explorar el mundo mítico del Universo Alebrijes y, para los interesados, la propiedad intelectual de Alebrijes® y Calaveras Linares® está disponible para incorporarla a sus proyectos creativos.

funds.name: Masterwork Fund for Objects of Awe
funds.subtitle: Seeking sovereign creators building awe-inspiring sculptures, paintings, installations, land art, and other ambitious masterpieces in the physical world.
funds.description: The Masterwork Fund supports sovereign creators pursuing ambitious works that transform imagination into reality. We believe masterpieces emerge when uncompromising artists dedicate themselves to a singular vision despite immense material challenges. From monumental sculptures and masterful paintings to kinetic installations, land art, handcrafted instruments, and other objects of awe, we champion creators building highly ambitious works in the physical world. Our mission is to help exceptional makers overcome the material bottlenecks standing between vision and execution.

funds.name: MCON Fund for Community Events
funds.subtitle: Seeking MCON community members to host events that bridge local and global perspectives, fostering a vibrant, inclusive DAO ecosystem.
funds.description:
The MCON Fund seeks project proposals for community events that connect members of the global MCON community with local blockchain groups, artists and musicians. By encouraging relationships between local cultural leaders and changemakers and the global MCON community, the fund aims to foster a vibrant ecosystem of knowledge sharing and collaborative innovation, enhancing the impact and reach of of DAO creators, enthusiasts, and innovators.
Note: Although events across the globe will be eligible for this fund, first consideration will be given to events in Detroit during the week of MCON, September 25-29th, 2024.

funds.name: MDRN Fund for Community Radio
funds.subtitle: Seeking community broadcasters connecting musicians and audiences through independent radio, podcasts, livestreams, and local music culture.
funds.description: The MDRN Fund for Community Radio supports the people building the future of independent music distribution. We believe community radio stations, online broadcasters, DIY venues, podcasts, and local music platforms are essential cultural infrastructure that help artists find audiences and communities discover one another. From neighborhood FM stations to internet-native radio collectives, we champion projects that strengthen local music ecosystems through broadcasting, collaboration, and shared ownership.

funds.name: Mental Wealth Fund
funds.subtitle: Spiritual Wealth. Open The Ethereal Horizon.
funds.description:
The Mental Wealth Fund is actively managed by an AI Agent.

funds.name: MetaCamp Regeneration Fund
funds.subtitle: Co-create projects that preserve culture and regenerate ecosystems.
funds.description: The MetaCamp Regeneration Fund aims to bridge the worlds of digital innovation and ancestral wisdom, fostering partnerships that respect and amplify the cultural and environmental stewardship of Costa Rica's indigenous peoples. This fund supports collaborative projects that integrate web3 technologies with traditional practices in areas such as conservation, arts, and community development, creating a shared space for learning, exchange, and mutual growth.

funds.name: Metacrisis Fund for Positive-Sum Interventions
funds.subtitle: Seeking positive-sum projects that address the generator functions of the metacrisis
funds.description:
Climate breakdown, AI risk, ecological collapse, institutional distrust, the loneliness epidemic — these look like separate emergencies competing for attention. They aren't. They're symptoms produced by a shared set of generator functions: rivalrous dynamics multiplied by exponential technology, economies that reward externalizing harm onto the commons and the future, and a collapse in our shared capacity to make sense of the world well enough to choose within it. Solve any one symptom while the generator functions keep running and they simply produce the next one.
This fund exists to support work on the generator functions themselves.
We back projects that make cooperation more rational than defection, that internalize externalities rather than displace them, that widen the circle of what participants are able to consider, and that increase our collective capacity for sensemaking and choice-making. That includes tools and infrastructure for collective sensemaking, media and art that build the perceptual and emotional capacities these problems demand, research on institutional and economic redesign, closed-loop material practices, and community-scale experiments in governance and care.
We're explicitly interested in the third attractor: a path between civilizational catastrophe on one side and stability purchased through surveillance and centralized control on the other. That path has to be built, and it will be built out of many small, legible, replicable experiments long before it looks like a system.
Most funding in this space goes to symptom management, because symptoms are measurable and generator functions are not. This fund accepts that tradeoff deliberately. We're matching support for the harder, slower, more upstream work.

funds.name: Metaverse Music Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting DJs, XR designers, and AI artists crafting the future of music in the metaverse.
funds.description: The Metaverse Music Fund supports artists and technologists pushing the boundaries of sound, performance, and space in the metaverse. From virtual venues to generative soundscapes, we fund projects that harness immersive technology to reimagine how music is created, shared, and experienced across digital realities.

funds.name: Microalgal Fund for Regenerative Futures
funds.subtitle: Supporting creators who work with microalgae to imagine, prototype, and share regenerative futures through art, science, and design.
funds.description: The Microalgal Fund for Regenerative Futures supports artists, scientists, designers, and entrepreneurs who engage microalgae as living collaborators in shaping life-supporting futures. We back work that reveals the quiet power, beauty, and strangeness of these microorganisms—translating microbiology and laboratory practice into public encounters and speculative design. From bioart and biodesign to food futures, biomaterials, and hands-on citizen science, this Fund supports projects that make microalgae legible, inspiring, and felt—inviting people to encounter them not as background life, but as partners in regenerative design.

funds.name: Mona Fund for 3D Creators
funds.subtitle: Empowering 3D creators to craft, launch, and sell original interoperable assets on MONA’s marketplace for the Open Metaverse.
funds.description: The MONA Match Fund is dedicated to supporting 3D creators shaping the Open Metaverse by producing original, interoperable assets. From avatars to environments, creators can leverage MONA’s tools to launch and sell their work to collectors and fans, fostering a thriving marketplace. Through this initiative, we aim to boost creative expression and drive adoption of high-quality 3D assets across diverse platforms.

funds.name: Motherland Fund for Rising Voices
funds.subtitle: We are seeking the spirit of Accra. Calling out to all creators who blend local heritage with global influence.
funds.description:
We support creators who are based in Accra or deeply connected to its cultural ecosystem, and who channel their local experiences into global conversations. To qualify for this fund, projects must meet the following eligibility requirements:
We are seeking projects that demonstrate a spirit of collaboration.
Project must span multidisciplinary fields: e.g. fashion, music, film, tech, photography, performance, and beyond.
Lead creator must be based in Accra & have strong, demonstrable ties to the city.
Project must reflect a “glocal” perspective—rooted in local culture with relevance or resonance beyond Accra.
Must demonstrate artistic excellence, creative innovation, and a commitment to community or cultural contribution.
Project should contribute to the growth, sustainability, or evolution of Accra’s creative economy.
Must align with Motherland’s values of Glocal Impact and Creative Nurturing from the Ground Up.

funds.name: MultiMax Fund for Immersive Interaction
funds.subtitle: For immersive, interactive projects that merge physical sensing and digital manipulation to create new forms of art.
funds.description: The MultiMax Fund for Immersive Interaction supports artists working across physical and digital modalities to build responsive, multisensory experiences. We champion projects that use sensors, microcontrollers, sound, light, and custom systems to translate human presence and environmental input into dynamic artistic expression. This fund exists to advance a new frontier of interactive art where audiences don’t just observe the work—they activate it.

funds.name: Mural Dreams Fund for Community Storytellers
funds.subtitle: Supporting muralists and street artists who turn public walls into powerful stories that uplift, inspire, and unite communities.
funds.description: The Mural Dreams Fund empowers artists who transform blank walls into cultural landmarks. We support muralists, street artists, illustrators, and youth creators who use public art to celebrate identity, beautify neighborhoods, and strengthen local pride. This Fund champions projects that bring people together through color, culture, and creative storytelling.

funds.name: NAIA Fund for Childhood Learning
funds.subtitle: Supporting visionary creators reimagining childhood education through nature, play, emotion, creativity, and purpose-driven technology.
funds.description: The NAIA Fund for Childhood Learning backs projects that restore joy, curiosity, and emotional wellbeing to education. From outdoor schools crafting nature-based curricula, to ethical AI tools enabling child-led exploration, to programs teaching emotional resilience, we support innovations that let every child learn in wonder, safety, and freedom.

funds.name: Nature's Voice Fund for Visual Storytelling
funds.subtitle: Funding visual stories told from nature's point of view.
funds.description: Nature cannot argue its own case, but stories can. This fund supports creators who use visual storytelling, film, animation, illustration, to give nature a voice and show the world from a non-human perspective: stories that build empathy, deepen understanding, and move people to care better for the natural world, made with the talent local to where each story lives.

funds.name: Neuro Chroma Fund for Nigeria's Next Generation
funds.subtitle: Supporting the rising generation of Nigerian creators fusing art and technology: AI artists, animators, manga makers, and game developers proving the future is already theirs.
funds.description: Named for a cyberpunk anime born in its own community and now living on Artizen, Neuro Chroma Fund is a statement from Nigeria's next generation of creators: we are capable of building futures as bold as anyone's. Across northern Nigeria and beyond, young artists are coming of age fluent in AI art, animation, manga, game design, VR, and film, brilliant, connected, and chronically overlooked by the institutions that fund creative work. This fund backs them at the intersection where art, science, and technology meet, and it's led by Ivan Ajidagba, a community organizer and Artizen creator who has spent years bringing together artists, designers, technologists, and cultural communities to experiment, learn from each other, and ship work that didn't wait for permission.

funds.name: Neuroarts Fund for Innerversal Health Practitioners
funds.subtitle: Supporting practitioners creating at the nexus of of sound medicine, somatic integration, and narrative self-expression.
funds.description:
Some of the most potent healing work happens between the lanes the funding world keeps separate, and this fund exists for the people building bridges there.
Neuroarts Fund for Innerversal Health Practitioners backs educators and practitioners creating phygital learning experiences, programs that live simultaneously in the body, the screen, and the room, spanning sound medicine, somatic integration, steeping arts, and narrative self-expression, made for people who've been told their knowledge and their ways of processing the world don't belong anywhere.
The fund is led by Kamau Zuberi Akabueze, who left a Chief Creative Officer career in 2022 to found THE ÅLïEN SCõÖL for Creative Thinking and has been building community platforms like CREÅTIVE STEEPING and the 1000 Ways to Sit series ever since; each year he'll invite the fund's creators to gather at Mars College, the site-built desert school in Bombay Beach, to mature their programs side by side. (More about this is ELIGIBILITY).
NeuroArtistry (the conjoined perspective) NeuroArtistry is an emergent practice that converges the science of how arts and aesthetic experiences reshape the brain, body, and behavior with the technology of deliberate creative self-engagement and the cartographic discipline of navigating the human being's internal universe, and how this convergence can be embodied by practitioners as a living methodology designed to advance the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.
This category of neuroscientific arts includes physical, mental, and social health, but also creative intelligence as an accessible relationship with our imagination, elevating the ecological contribution of a practitioner's own creative expression to the vibratory resonance that surround them. NeuroArtistry supports the ongoing movement from creative dislocation toward ecological integration.
Innerversal Health Practicum studies the architecture of the human being's internal universe — the innerversal — and trains practitioners in the instruments, cartographies, and awareness practices required to navigate our innerworlds with precision, translating this inner capacity into programs designed to advance the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities, including physical and mental wellness.
Steeping Arts is an interdisciplinary practice that studies the science of how deliberate, temperature-sensitive, time-aware engagement with one's own creative material — through expressive writing, music-induced emotional activation, and embodied inquiry — reorganizes how the nervous system parses creative experience, and how this knowledge can be translated into explorative rituals designed to advance creative fluency and ecological wellbeing of individuals and communities. The Steeping arts elevate our capacity for sustained somatic attention, and the practitioner's ecological contribution to the resonant fields that surround them.
::
Should your project touch any of these areas specifically, and or you steward a project that aspires to act on these emerging sciences and practices, please do apply.

funds.name: Neurodivergent Builders Fund
funds.subtitle: Seeking neurodivergent creators building products, technology, and creative work for neurodivergent people.
funds.description: The Neurodivergent Builders Fund supports founders, artists, designers, and creators transforming lived neurodivergent experience into products, tools, and creative work that make life more accessible, empowering, and joyful. We believe some of the world's most important innovations emerge from people who experience it differently. From AI and assistive technology to accessibility software, creative projects, and consumer products, we champion builders creating products and experiences specifically for neurodivergent people.

funds.name: Neurotech Fund for Evolving Consciousness
funds.subtitle: Putting real brain-computer interfaces in the hands of the people most likely to do something beautiful with them.
funds.description: For decades, brain-computer interfaces have lived in labs and pitch decks. Meanwhile artists, researchers, and toolmakers have been quietly turning real-time brain activity into visual art, sound, performance, and contemplative practice. This fund backs projects where neurotech is a genuine, working part of the work: BCI-driven live performance and visual art, research into consciousness and meditation, open tools that make brain interfaces accessible, and programs that bring the technology into contemplative and community spaces.

funds.name: Next Play Fund for Student-Athletes
funds.subtitle: Fueling businesses and initiatives led by or built for student-athletes preparing for life beyond college sports.
funds.description: The Next Play Fund supports projects that help student-athletes transition from the playing field to their next chapter as founders, innovators, and community leaders. Whether you're building a startup, launching a creative venture, or designing tools that support athlete well-being and success beyond sports, this fund exists to back your vision. We’re here for the builders helping student-athletes play—and win—the long game.

funds.name: Nightshift Fund for Working Artists
funds.subtitle: Direct support for musicians and filmmakers of striking artistic quality who work second jobs to survive.
funds.description:
This one is for the artists who pour their hearts into their craft while their time is eaten up by nightshifts and side jobs. Nightshift Fund offers unconditional income for those kindhearted artists who make music, art, and films of remarkable quality and refuse exploitative industry structures.
The Nightshift Fund exists to be that difference, and to become a home on Artizen for working class artists everywhere, starting with musicians and filmmakers. It prioritizes artists who do not earn a living income from their art, and looks for community-centered, DIY, non-exploitative practice. Artistic quality is reviewed by a jury of fellow artists, because the people best placed to recognize the work are the ones making it.

funds.name: Nouns Africa Fund for IRL Education & Ecosystem Building
funds.subtitle: Funding Africa-based builders, educators, and creatives strengthening the Nouns Africa ecosystem through in-person education, public goods, and onchain culture.
funds.description: The Nouns Africa Fund for IRL Education & Ecosystem Building supports projects emerging from Africa’s growing Nouns ecosystem—spanning education, community building, public goods, and onchain culture. While education remains central, this fund welcomes in-person initiatives that onboard new participants, strengthen local capacity, and grow onchain culture through real-world engagement. Curated projects that successfully raise at least $100 for their IRL initiative will receive one Nouns DAO Africa NFT at the end of the season, recognizing their contribution to education, creativity, and ecosystem growth across the continent. Led by Nouns DAO Africa, this fund reflects deep, on-the-ground experience supporting builders and communities across Africa.

funds.name: Nouns Builder Fund for Onchain Communities
funds.subtitle: Supporting builders who strengthen the infrastructure, tools, and experiments that help onchain communities launch, govern, and grow with Nouns Builder.
funds.description: The Nouns Builder Fund for Onchain Communities supports projects that expand the utility, sustainability, and creative potential of the Nouns Builder ecosystem. We’re looking for builders developing tools, integrations, governance improvements, auction innovations, and other public infrastructure that help communities coordinate onchain more effectively and grow with greater flexibility, participation, and resilience.

funds.name: OASA Village Fund
funds.subtitle: Backing villages that hold land in common, restore ecosystems by hand, and pioneer new ways of governing together.
funds.description: A new kind of village is taking root. Communities of all sizes are holding land in common, restoring soils and water cycles with their own hands, and testing new forms of governance built on open tools. The OASA Village Fund backs these solarpunk settlements: places that treat land as a living commons rather than a speculative asset. The model is already working at Traditional Dream Factory in Portugal, the network's first village, where a community stewards shared land through a legal token structure. This fall, we are building a cohort of 10 villages that align in values with OASA and are willing to try our tools and grow together. Each one a working experiment in regeneration, self-governance, and shared ownership, and each one proof that a regenerative future is buildable now. The fund also grows from within: when villages use Closer for bookings, a 4% fee on commercial transactions goes to developing the platform, and 1% is put back into this fund to grow and support the network.

funds.name: Ocean Art & Media Fund
funds.subtitle: Seeking ocean-centered artists, storytellers, and founders whose work inspires people to protect and preserve the sea.
funds.description: The Ocean Art & Media Fund supports photographers, painters, filmmakers, writers, marine artists, and mission-aligned founders whose work is rooted in the sea. We back projects that turn awe into stewardship—celebrating ocean beauty, confronting threats like pollution, reef loss, and overfishing, and moving audiences to protect the blue heart of our planet.

funds.name: Ocean Fund for Living Seas
funds.subtitle: Funding creative, community-led science and culture projects that protect and monitor marine ecosystems in coastal regions.
funds.description: The Ocean Fund for Living Seas empowers coastal communities advancing ocean stewardship through science, local knowledge, culture, and open technology. From reef and megafauna monitoring to community storytelling and low-cost conservation tools, we support creators restoring the living seas that sustain us all.

funds.name: ODIN Fund for Decentralized Innovation
funds.subtitle: Funding open, decentralized projects reinventing how people collaborate, govern, and innovate together.
funds.description: The ODIN Fund for Decentralized Innovation supports creators building the next generation of open, self-managed communities and innovation networks. We believe the world’s hardest problems will be solved by decentralized groups that share knowledge, distribute power, and collaborate across boundaries. This fund backs open-source tools, playbooks, and experiments that help communities coordinate effectively, build trust, and scale innovation through shared ownership and evolutionary organizational practices.

funds.name: OLTA Fund for Interactive Art
funds.subtitle: Seeking creators to transform interactive art
funds.description:
Imagine art that is ever-changing, evolving over time. Art that is more social, open ended and inclusive. Where audiences actively engage and become an integral part of an artistic concept, or story layer. Art that you can invite people to contribute, co-create, and leave their mark, before, during or after an event. Art that is interactive and networked, that persists for generations. Art that reflects the world around us.
The OLTA Fund for Interactive Art seeks creators who value both permanence and participation, who love to create projects that leave a lasting impression. We’d love to support a community of digital creatives to create interactive art, design, music, or story projects, using our toolkit, then together launch the projects into the wild to foster connections through collective experiences.

funds.name: Open Health Fund
funds.subtitle: A greenhouse, not a gate: funding the edge of health innovation that fits no traditional bucket.
funds.description: The most interesting health work often happens at the edges: biohackers building their own diagnostics, patient communities developing solutions for their own conditions, open-source developers creating health data platforms, engineers building decentralized AI for medical imaging. These projects are too healthcare for infrastructure funds, too applied for academic grants, too early for venture capital. Open Health Fund is a greenhouse for them: nurturing early-stage health projects until they can stand on their own, whether that means spinning out as a startup, entering clinical practice, or becoming permanent open infrastructure.

funds.name: Open Infrastructure Fund for Human Coordination
funds.subtitle: Seeking open source engineers and researchers building the infrastructure that enables trust, coordination, and collective intelligence.
funds.description: The Open Infrastructure Fund for Human Coordination supports builders creating the systems that make large-scale human collaboration possible. We believe the future of AI, digital identity, decentralized coordination, and public goods should be built on open infrastructure that belongs to everyone rather than controlled by a handful of institutions. This fund champions open source protocols, privacy-preserving technologies, and shared digital infrastructure that enable the next generation of human creativity, scientific discovery, and collective intelligence.

funds.name: Open Music Fund for Sovereign Sound Builders
funds.subtitle: Supporting the builders of open music infrastructure: tools, instruments, and models that put artists above platforms.
funds.description: The tools that could make music fairer almost never get built: too unprofitable for venture capital, too strange for traditional grants, too honest about who the streaming economy actually serves. Open Music Fund exists for exactly those builders: open-source plugins and production tools, community radio and sonic commons, cassette-revival hardware, digital instruments, collaborative songwriting platforms, cooperative labels, and programmable royalties that distribute value transparently. The fund is led by Sol Siete and 0xGonzalo, co-founders of MúsicaW3, a Latin American community that has spent four years building toward a more sovereign music industry, creating the direct-to-fan platform Shine, hosting hundreds of educational broadcasts, and staging onchain exhibitions and festivals from Mexico to Thailand, guided by a conviction sharpened on the industry's periphery: technology only matters insofar as it puts artists above platforms and speculation.

funds.name: OpenCivics Fund for Resilient Communities
funds.subtitle: Empowering projects that drive civic innovation and foster collective stewardship.
funds.description: The OpenCivics Fund supports projects that drive civic innovation, enhancing the collective stewardship of our communities. We fund initiatives in infrastructure, technology, social processes, and educational curricula that enable active citizen engagement and holistic well-being. By promoting resilience, choice, and vitality, our aim is to create public goods that benefit all members of society, fostering a democratic and thriving civic life.

funds.name: Orion Fund for Living Intelligence
funds.subtitle: Supporting creators who build enduring systems of knowledge and decision-making that help humanity navigate long-term risk.
funds.description: The Orion Fund for Living Intelligence supports creators who build work designed to help humanity think more clearly across time. We seek projects grounded in living intelligence: systems that deepen how humans observe the world, make decisions, and steward complex realities. This includes ontological design, decision systems, ecological sensing, and regenerative knowledge infrastructure that address long-term human risk. The fund celebrates slow knowledge—work created for durability and clarity rather than speed or visibility—and supports creators willing to take responsibility for ideas meant to endure.

funds.name: Pachamama Fund for Living Culture
funds.subtitle: Supporting musicians, dancers, filmmakers, and tradition bearers whose work turns strangers into friends and audiences into communities.
funds.description: For more than fifty years, Quentin Navia has built creative community the old way: live, together, night after night. As co-founder of SUKAY she carried Andean music from Carnegie Hall to Red Rocks, and for the past 27 years she and her husband, two-time Latin Grammy nominee Eddy Navia, have run Peña Pachamama, the San Francisco Legacy Business where emerging artists perform beside master musicians and, as one guest put it after stepping through the door, you enter another order of reality. This fund extends that stage to the world: backing artists who preserve cultural heritage while creating new experiences of connection across cultures and generations, because every community deserves places where beauty, imagination, and generosity flourish together.

funds.name: PAM CUT Fund for the Storytellers of Tomorrow
funds.subtitle: Empowering visionary creators shaping the future of cinematic, immersive, and multidisciplinary storytelling.
funds.description: The PAM CUT Fund for the Storytellers of Tomorrow supports creators worldwide who are redefining what cinema can be—across film, XR, immersive media, animation, performance, audio stories, and hybrid forms. Rooted in Portland’s vibrant media-arts ecosystem, PAM CUT champions artists pushing the boundaries of storytelling and invites them to bring groundbreaking work to life through exhibition at its world-class venues.

funds.name: Paradigm Fund for Frontier Tech
funds.subtitle: Supporting early builders creating the invisible technologies that will become the foundation of everyday human life.
funds.description: The Paradigm Fund for Frontier Tech supports early-stage builders working at the edges of AI, biotech, robotics, and blockchain—technologies destined to fade into the background precisely because they work so well. We back projects that prioritize direct human impact over enterprise utility, focusing on tools that quietly improve life, expand agency, and strengthen society. This fund exists to give overlooked builders the runway to turn working ideas into foundational infrastructure for the future.

funds.name: Paradiseön Fund for Art, Earth & Regeneration
funds.subtitle: Seeking artists, Indigenous creators, storytellers, and community builders cultivating a more beautiful, regenerative world.
funds.description:
The paradiseön Fund supports creators who help people remember that paradise is not a distant destination—it is something we create together. We believe art, music, storytelling, technology, and community can deepen our relationship with Mother Earth and inspire people to protect the living world. From Indigenous cultural preservation and ecological storytelling to regenerative technology, public art, music, and community gatherings, we champion creators whose work nurtures life, beauty, and belonging. We believe paradise is not a place. It is a collaborative artwork, and this fund exists to support the creators bringing it to life.
More Informations @ www.paradiseon.earth

funds.name: Phygital Performance Fund for Immersive Art
funds.subtitle: Supporting artists at the frontier of live performance, immersive technology, and phygital art—presented at Carriageworks, Sydney.
funds.description: The Phygital Performance Fund for Immersive Art supports emerging and established artists working across physical performance and digital technologies, from interactive installations to live, 360-degree experiences. Led by Box of Birds in partnership with Carriageworks, the fund is anchored in Bay 19, a large-scale, technically advanced presentation space in Sydney. Through curated salons, showcases, and installations, the fund provides artists with access to professional-grade projection, sound, tracking, and performance infrastructure, fostering experimentation, exchange, and public engagement around the future of immersive performance.

funds.name: Plato Fund for Local Flavor
funds.subtitle: Seeking creative projects to help revitalize mom-and-pop restaurants.
funds.description:
The Plato Match Fund aims to rejuvenate local, community-centric restaurants by funding projects that creatively boost in-person foot traffic. In partnership with Plato Eats, a restaurant loyalty dApp, we believe that mom-and-pop eateries form the backbone of local communities. Our mission is to ignite innovative collaborations between creators and their favorite restaurants to revitalize these spaces as hubs of culture, creativity, and community engagement. By doing so, we will help local restaurants not just survive, but flourish as vibrant hubs of social and cultural interaction.
📖 Read Essay: Get Funded to Revive Local Flavor

funds.name: Plural Events Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding the local sessions of global conversations: one topic, many places, many perspectives.
funds.description: Plural events flip the conference model: instead of one stage, the same topic is discussed in real-life groups in many locations around the same time, and the perspectives are gathered into a more plural understanding than any single room could produce. Inspired by Audrey Tang and Glen Weyl's plurality principles, this fund supports the individual in-person sessions that make up each Plural event, conversations about society's structures, democracy, privacy, and technology, hosted in independent spaces around the world.

funds.name: Podcast Fund for Emerging Voices
funds.subtitle: Seeking podcast and radio projects from independent storytellers sharing art, culture, and lived experience.
funds.description: The Podcast Fund for Emerging Voices supports independent creators using audio to tell original stories across art, culture, and lived experience. We champion writers, artists, performers, and cultural observers outside big media systems who bring distinct points of view, collaborative spirit, and living voices to the world.

funds.name: Portland Fund for Grassroots Regeneration
funds.subtitle: Funding DIY regeneration through permaculture, art, and placemaking to make Portland more beautiful, edible, and alive.
funds.description: Portland is full of people that are focused on rewilding, urban food production, community repair, and creative placemaking—yet many lack the resources to bring their visions to life. The Portland Fund for Grassroots Regeneration provides micro-grants to these grassroots visionaries who are transforming our city one vacant lot, street corner, and neighborhood at a time. We support projects that center artistic placemaking and ecological regeneration: food forests emerging from cracked concrete, pollinator havens brightening forgotten spaces, community murals that bring neighbors together. With a no-red-tape approach, we're backing the solarpunks, guerrilla gardeners, and community artists who aren't waiting for permission to create a more beautiful, resilient Portland. If your project feeds people, restores ecology, or sparks joy—the Portland Fund for Grassroots Regeneration wants to help make it happen!

funds.name: Pressman Film Fund for New Frontiers
funds.subtitle: Supporting the next generation of filmmakers exploring the frontier of storytelling through emerging technology.
funds.description: For more than five decades, Pressman Film has championed daring voices at the edge of culture—long before they were considered canon. Films like Das Boot, Badlands, Wall Street, American Psycho, and Thank You for Smoking were once frontier works by bold, unconventional storytellers. Through Press 3, Pressman’s newly formed subsidiary, that same independent spirit now extends beyond the traditional frame—supporting artists working in emerging narrative forms across immersive media, AI-driven storytelling, and technology-native experiences. This Fund seeks projects that honor cinematic craft while pushing storytelling into new territory, building the next generation of frontier works for audiences wherever stories are headed.

funds.name: Proof of Craic Fund for Harm Reduction
funds.subtitle: Giving a voice to those excluded from building policies that directly affect them
funds.description:
❤️‍🩹 In Ireland, harm reduction is often talked about but rarely funded.
The Proof of Craic Fund is rooted in harm reduction and symbolic resistance. It begins with Molly Malone’s statue — a sex worker immortalised in the heart of Dublin, her bronze boobies worn shiny by tourists for ‘luck’.
But her bronze boobies are no joke. They’re a mirror.
While statues get polished and protected, real women — especially SWers — are suffering under performative policies.
🤕 WTF is harm reduction?
Harm reduction is a public good (yes, jargon). Everyone should be able to enjoy reduced harm in a non-excludable and non-rivalrous way. We can do that through designing and funding:
📖 Counter-narratives that shift public perception
😮‍💨 Mental health and burnout support
⚖️ Gender-inclusive, care-first public systems

funds.name: Radical Movers Fund for Contact Improv
