funds.subtitle: A fund for Contact Improvisation projects advancing accessibility, decolonial practice, and community.
funds.description:
The Contact Improvisation Fund for Radical Movers supports artists, organizers, facilitators, researchers, collectives, and community practitioners using Contact Improvisation as a practice of social transformation rather than simply a dance form. We fund projects that expand access, strengthen locally rooted communities, cultivate collective care, and explore how embodied practice can respond to questions of justice, ecology, migration, disability, gender, and power.
Some of the most important work in Contact Improvisation is happening far from the best-known festivals: in grassroots communities from La Havana to Goa to Busan, where movement and radical playfulness become ways of reimagining how people live together on this shared planet. Yet these initiatives are often underfunded and overlooked. This fund seeks to redistribute not only financial resources, but also visibility, trust, and recognition toward the people building resilient, community-rooted practices.
The fund is led by fran and Fer, two long-standing community organisers deeply embedded in international Contact Improvisation networks across Europe, Asia and Abya Yala. Together, they work as connectors between communities, helping circulate knowledge, relationships, and resources horizontally while supporting practices that remain accountable to their own local territories. The fund aims to strengthen this global ecology by investing in the people already imagining more accessible, decolonial, and socially engaged futures for Contact Improvisation.

funds.name: Radical Responsibility Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding the physical foundations of the next culture.
funds.description:
The Radical Responsibility Fund supports edge-walkers and culture creators who refuse to wait for permission and are actively building the next culture in real life.
We support people creating regenerative villages, physical communities, and living experiments where new ways of living, organising, relating, learning, and collaborating can be tested, developed, and embodied.
We believe that new culture cannot survive only as an idea.
It needs land.
It needs places.
It needs homes, gathering spaces, gardens, workshops, kitchens, learning environments and social infrastructure.
It needs real humans with real stakes learning how to live differently together.
The Radical Responsibility Fund is a tailwind for those building these prototypes.
These are projects creating physical regenerative villages and communities: places where people are not simply talking about alternatives to extractive and hierarchical systems, but actively inventing and practising them.
These are living laboratories for cultural evolution.
Places where people can experiment with new forms of governance, education, family, community, relationship, economics, regeneration and collaboration with Earth.
At the heart of the fund is Radical Responsibility: the understanding that we are not powerless victims waiting for someone else to fix the world.
We are the creators, we don't need permission and nobody is going to create the world we want to live in for us.
We support projects rooted in self-authorship, accountability, agency and the willingness to be changed by the experiments they are creating.
We are interested in communities that use innovative human technologies (facilitation, training, conscious feelings work, emotional literacy, ritual, initiation, coaching and other consciousness-based practices) to develop the capacity required for humans to collaborate.
Because building beautiful infrastructure is not enough.
The greatest infrastructure challenge is often human.
How do we live together?
How do we stay in relationship when things get difficult?
How do we make decisions without simply recreating hierarchy?
How do we raise children, steward land, share resources and create together without reproducing the systems we are trying to leave behind?
The Radical Responsibility Fund exists to fertilise living experiments exploring these questions.
We want to support the creation of villages that can become seeds for more villages.
Prototypes that can be learned from, adapted and multiplied.
Places where people can come not only to visit, but to train as regenerative village makers and carry what they learn into the creation of new communities elsewhere.
We are moving toward a world of villages of villages: networks of autonomous, regenerative communities, each with its own character and culture, connected through shared learning, research and evolution.
We are not looking for perfect utopias.
We are looking for real experiments.
Messy, courageous, alive places where people are willing to take responsibility for what they are creating and discover, through lived experience, what actually works.
Our aim is not simply to imagine the next culture.
It is to build places where it can exist.

funds.name: Reactor Fund for Hardcore Hackers
funds.subtitle: Fueling the fearless creators who weld, hack, machine, solder, explode, and rebuild the physical world from their garages and homemade labs.
funds.description:
This Fund backs backs mad scientists
If you machine rocket nozzles , resurrect surplus vacuum systems, print custom PCBs have a diy sintering system or shoot electrons through DIY accelerators lfg

funds.name: Reciprocity Fund for Indigenous Creators
funds.subtitle: A ReziDAO initiative uplifting Indigenous creators using ancestral knowledge and emergent tech to foster cultural and economic sovereignty.
funds.description: Launched by ReziDAO, the Reciprocity Fund supports Indigenous artists and technologists weaving traditional knowledge with regenerative tools to strengthen community, culture, and sovereignty. This Fund champions visionary creators whose work reclaims Indigenous futures through innovation and kinship-rooted design.

funds.name: ReFi Fund for Regenerative Initiatives
funds.subtitle: Helping regenerative projects evolve from survival to thriving, from grant-dependent to economically resilient.
funds.description: The people restoring ecosystems, building regenerative food and energy systems, and strengthening community governance are rarely chasing wealth; they are answering a calling. Too many remain trapped in survival mode, unable to grow their impact or build stable livelihoods. This fund is infrastructure for that work: it supports regenerative initiatives with real, measurable impact that are on a credible path toward economic self-sufficiency beyond grant funding, honoring both the planet and the people brave enough to restore it.

funds.name: Refraction Fund for Art + Public Goods
funds.subtitle: Fueling Art that Powers Public Goods
funds.description: How do public goods get funded, and why does it matter? The Refraction Fund for Art + Public Goods, sponsored by Gitcoin, empowers artists to make these complex systems visible and engaging. From dynamic visual storytelling to interactive installations, this fund supports creative projects that illustrate mechanism design, demonstrate funding flows, and reveal the real-world impact of public goods—bridging the gap between technology, art, and collective action.

funds.name: Refraction Fund for IRL Culture
funds.subtitle: Fueling art and music projects that use digital and onchain creativity to bring people together in real life.
funds.description: The Refraction Fund for IRL Culture supports creators using digital tools, onchain systems, and networked art or music to spark real-world gatherings, rituals, and shared cultural moments. We champion bold projects that merge online innovation with IRL connection to build vibrant, participatory culture for the communities they touch.

funds.name: Regen Coordination Fund
funds.subtitle: Resourcing the networks that connect regenerative communities across chapters, nodes, and bioregions worldwide.
funds.description: The Regen Coordination Fund supports the networks weaving the regenerative movement together. We back umbrella networks whose chapters, nodes, and member communities span cities and bioregions worldwide, and who create the spaces, online and in person, where people connect, collaborate, and launch regenerative initiatives. The fund also resources curated initiatives emerging directly from Regen Coordination, like the Regen Toolkit, that provide shared infrastructure for these networks. Stewarded by Regen Coordination, an alliance including ReFi DAO and Greenpill Network that has distributed over $370K to regenerative projects, this fund pools support so that coordination itself gets resourced, not just the projects it makes possible.

funds.name: Regenerative Materials Fund for Convivial Building
funds.subtitle: Funding straw, hemp, earth, and timber building, and the teaching that lets communities own the skill.
funds.description: Buildings should come from the land and return to it, and the knowledge of how to make them should belong to the people who live in them. This fund supports builders, architects, material scientists, and educators developing regenerative, bio-based, low-toxicity building materials and methods, straw, hemp, earth, timber, reclaimed and renewable materials, with an emphasis on convivial tools: techniques simple and transparent enough that a community can learn, repair, and adapt them on their own terms, free from permanent dependence on outside suppliers and experts.

funds.name: Regenerative Village Culture Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding live-in village projects growing the inner and relational skills that let people actually live, decide, and create together.
funds.description: Land, buildings, and gardens do not make a village. People do, and people arrive carrying wounds, projections, and unfinished emotions that can quietly take a whole project down. The Regenerative Village Culture Fund backs live-in village projects, temporary or long-term, that treat this human layer as the real work: groups practising emotional responsibility, non-hierarchical decision-making, shadow and underworld work, adulthood initiation, and shared learning while actually living together. Where other funds build the physical foundations of the next culture, this one grows the relational ones, the skills that let a group stay in relationship when things get difficult and make living together more alive than living alone. Funded projects share what they discover with the wider global village, so each experiment becomes a map for the next. Not a utopian fantasy. Real people, under one roof, learning to live and create together.

funds.name: ReNature the City Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting creative projects that reimagine cities as living ecosystems
funds.description:
A flower breaking through asphalt is a small revolution.
ReNature the City supports community-led projects that bring ecological life, climate resilience, biodiversity, and human wellbeing back into urban space.
We are interested in the people imagining new ways for cities to coexist with water, soil, plants, animals, fungi, and each other.
This can take the form of a rain garden absorbing stormwater, a stream freed from concrete, a native micro-forest cooling a neighborhood, a food garden transforming idle land, or a green corridor reconnecting fragmented habitats.
But it can also be something less conventional: a project creating habitat for urban wildlife, an artistic intervention that changes how people perceive a neglected ecosystem, a community experiment reconnecting people with nature, a new approach to urban biodiversity, or a technology helping cities understand and restore living systems.
We are especially interested in projects that challenge the idea that cities exist only for humans.
What happens when birds, insects, trees, rivers, fungi, soil and people are all considered part of the same urban system?
We believe that restoring these relationships can make cities more resilient to climate change, richer in biodiversity, and healthier places to live, including for our mental and emotional wellbeing.
Supports the people already experimenting with these possibilities: landscape designers, ecologists, artists, grassroots architects, scientists, technologists, educators, gardeners, and neighborhood collectives.
Renaturing a city is about more than planting trees.
It is about changing our relationship with the living world around us.
Imagine living cities
ReNature the City

funds.name: Render Fund for Decentralized Creativity
funds.subtitle: Supporting projects that expand the Render Network and empowering creators who transform the future of digital art.
funds.description: The Render Fund, powered by the Render Network Foundation, is dedicated to growing a vibrant ecosystem of creators and developers harnessing the power of decentralized GPU rendering. By connecting idle GPU compute power with innovative projects, the Render Network is transforming digital creation—enabling unmatched efficiency, scale, and creative freedom. This match fund empowers artists, developers, and visionaries to push the boundaries of 3D rendering and AI-powered applications, fostering a future where creativity is accessible to all.

funds.name: Resonate Fund for Sonic Pioneers
funds.subtitle: Backing new voices in music by amplifying creators who challenge industry gatekeepers and redefine how sound is made, shared, and heard.
funds.description: The Resonate Fund is for musicians, composers, and sonic innovators who are creating new music and new forms of sound . Founded by Scott Murphy—a lifelong musician and audio engineer—the fund invests in talent often overlooked by traditional institutions. In addition to funding, selected creators gain access to a professional recording studio and performance space at Frontier Tower in San Francisco. We believe in amplifying original voices and reshaping the future of sound.

funds.name: Revīv Fund for Nourishing Mothers
funds.subtitle: Supporting creators and caregivers restoring mother-centered postpartum care through nourishment, education, community, and restorative support systems.
funds.description: The Revīv Fund for Nourishing Mothers supports creators, caregivers, and community builders helping restore the culture of care that has historically surrounded mothers after birth. We seek projects that nourish, educate, and support women through the postpartum transition—through workshops, storytelling, bodywork, food systems, practical resources, and community-driven care models that help rebuild the village around motherhood.

funds.name: ReWoven Fund for Regenerative Communities and Media
funds.subtitle: Funding regenerative projects and the bioregional storytellers embedded with them, so every build becomes a story that spreads.
funds.description: The regenerative movement is rich in projects and starved for storytellers. Ecovillages transform, land comes home, new ways of living get built, and almost none of it is documented well enough to spread. We believe people choose a regenerative life when they can see one: awareness, access, and the capacity to move through fear, and storytelling advances all three at once. Born from ReWoven, the intentional community makeover show piloted at Liminal Village in Italy, this fund backs regenerative projects, land-based or digital, along with the bioregional filmmakers, reweaving consultants, and educational spaces that grow the network around them. Every funded project includes a paid storyteller, so each grant builds the work and the storyteller layer at the same time. Nothing regenerative should happen unwitnessed.

funds.name: ReWoven Fund for Regenerative Communities and Media
funds.subtitle: Funding regenerative projects and the bioregional storytellers embedded with them, so every build becomes a story that spreads.
funds.description: The regenerative movement is rich in projects and starved for storytellers. Ecovillages transform, land comes home, new ways of living get built, and almost none of it is documented well enough to spread. We believe people choose a regenerative life when they can see one: awareness, access, and the capacity to move through fear, and storytelling advances all three at once. Born from ReWoven, the intentional community makeover show piloted at Liminal Village in Italy, this fund backs regenerative projects, land-based or digital, along with the bioregional filmmakers, reweaving consultants, and educational spaces that grow the network around them. Every funded project includes a paid storyteller, so each grant builds the work and the storyteller layer at the same time. Nothing regenerative should happen unwitnessed.

funds.name: Rising Voices of Cascadia Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting on-the-rise musicians and creators from the Cascadia region to produce genre-bending albums, immersive concerts, and inclusive art experiences.
funds.description: The Rising Voices of Cascadia Fund celebrates the creative vibrancy of the Pacific Northwest by uplifting underrepresented musicians and multidisciplinary artists from the Seattle and broader Cascadia bioregion. Hosted by a collective of staff, volunteers, and artists, this Fund champions projects that spark collaboration, bridge communities, and create space for all to connect through the beauty of live music and art.

funds.name: Riviera Maya Regenerative Futures Fund
funds.subtitle: Backing the artists, scientists, and community leaders regenerating the Riviera Maya and the Mesoamerican Reef bioregion, culture and ecology together.
funds.description: The Riviera Maya sits where the jungle meets the second largest reef system on Earth. Cenotes feed the aquifer, mangroves hold the coast, and Maya culture runs through all of it. It is also one of the fastest-developing coastlines in the Americas, and the people restoring it are usually the last to be resourced. The Riviera Maya Regenerative Futures Fund backs projects rooted in this bioregion: artists and filmmakers telling its stories, scientists and regenerative innovators restoring reef, mangrove, and forest, educators and community leaders weaving people back into place. Curated by ReFi Tulum, a community that gathers residents and visitors around cleanups, plantings, coral work, and regenerative cultural experiences, the fund is being built with its community, not just for it: projects, co-curators, and sponsors shape the pool together. The reef is one living system, from cenote to coral. So is the culture that cares for it.

funds.name: Rooted in Reciprocity Fund
funds.subtitle: Expanding access to self-directed, nature-based learning for children, families, and communities.
funds.description: Learning is not confined to four walls or a standardized path; it is alive, and it grows through caring mentors, meaningful experiences, and a deep relationship with the places we call home. Rooted in Reciprocity Fund supports educators, mentors, artists, naturalists, and community leaders creating immersive, self-directed, nature-based learning, and works to make those experiences accessible to every child and family, regardless of income, background, learning differences, or circumstance. At its heart is reciprocity: the understanding that we are not separate from one another or the living world, and that every action can contribute, restore, and inspire.

funds.name: Scout Game Fund for Open Source Builders
funds.subtitle: Empowering open source developers who are building the decentralized future of blockchain public goods.
funds.description: The Scout Game Fund supports open source developers advancing public goods in the blockchain ecosystem. Whether you're building foundational onchain infrastructure, decentralized apps, or AI-powered agents for Web3, this Fund backs projects that champion transparency, collaboration, and innovation. Let’s code the commons and build the decentralized tools the world needs.

funds.name: Scribe Fund for Storytellers
funds.subtitle: Seeking writers, storytellers, and world-builders creating books that inspire regenerative futures and cultivate new cultural myths.
funds.description: The Scribe Fund for Storytellers supports writers who weave stories, legends, and knowledge that help humanity imagine and embody new ways of living. We believe books are among the most powerful technologies for cultural transformation. Through novels, anthologies, scripts, comic books, and other written works, this fund seeks to nurture voices that expand our collective imagination, preserve wisdom, and illuminate regenerative futures. Our mission is to cultivate a thriving ecosystem of storytellers whose words inspire more connected, resilient, and life-affirming cultures.

funds.name: Scroll Fund for the Open Economy
funds.subtitle: Fueling the next generation of decentralized applications that make the Open Economy more scalable, secure, and accessible for all.
funds.description: The Scroll Fund for the Open Economy supports developers building on Scroll’s zero-knowledge rollup to create dApps that drive Ethereum’s scalability and adoption. By leveraging Scroll’s zkEVM, projects can lower costs, improve performance, and expand access to decentralized finance, digital ownership, and beyond. Whether you’re building DeFi protocols, NFT marketplaces, or new blockchain infrastructure, we’re here to help bring your vision to life.

funds.name: SheFi Fund for Web3 Pioneers
funds.subtitle: Empowering women to master Web3, launch their careers, and shape the future of frontier technologies.
funds.description: At SheFi, we believe the frontier is feminine. The SheFi Fund provides scholarships to help cover the program fee for women eager to join the SheFi cohort and funding for innovative projects created during and after the program. By supporting education, experimentation, and community-building, this fund enables women to master Web3, reinvent their careers, and build transformative solutions in blockchain and beyond.

funds.name: Si Her Fund for Womxn in Web3
funds.subtitle: A global collaborative of 50+ womxn-led Web3 communities & leaders driving the next wave of Web3 adoption.
funds.description:
Si Her DAO is a decentralizing collaborative of womxn-led communities and leaders. Our DAO is uniting 50 (and growing) womxn-led communities spanning the globe from Nigeria to Mexico to Hong Kong. With every continent represented, we are demonstrating decentralization through real-world application.
As an active, interconnected web of global womxn leaders, we each bring our own unique talents and cultures to a shared vision of bringing womxn into leadership in the new economy.
This fund is the kickoff to our DAO fund, which brings economic and human resources to global, Web3-focused, womxn-led projects and communities.
Our intention with this kickoff fund is to support projects and communities in reaching their next phase of growth and further unite our individual and shared missions. We aim to break silos and weave an interconnected web of outstanding projects, communities, and professionals.
This fund is led by Kara Howard, a womxn-in-emerging tech community leader of 13 years whose career spans from Wall Street finance to Silicon Valley tech to Web3.
To learn more about Si Her DAO, explore here: https://si3.space/dao

funds.name: Solar Regeneration Fund for Nigerian Creatives
funds.subtitle: Funding solar-powered, connected hubs across Nigeria where young musicians, filmmakers, and builders can finally make and share their work.
funds.description: Across Nigeria the power fails, the internet fails with it, and every creative project pays the price: a film that cannot upload, a track that cannot render, a class that drops mid-lesson. The Solar Regeneration Fund for Nigerian Creatives backs the young people fixing this from the ground up. Student collectives turning shipping containers and campus rooms into solar-powered, Starlink-connected studios. Self-taught solar technicians and welders who build the systems and publish how they did it. And the musicians, filmmakers, designers, and climate and Web3 educators who fill those rooms with work. The model already runs: at Nnamdi Azikiwe University in Awka, a 20-foot container hub on six solar panels and a 7.2 kWh battery bank serves the campus community of musicians, coders, and builders. Every funded hub documents its build openly on Green Goods so the next team starts from a working recipe instead of scratch. The hub is the venue. The creators are the point.

funds.name: Solarpunk Futures Fund
funds.subtitle: Empowering Regen rebels to envision renewable futures —where Solarpunk ideals meet Pirate codes
funds.description: We champion creators who fuse the radical optimism of Solarpunk with the rebellious self-governance of the Pirate Codes. Solarpunk envisions a future where humanity thrives in harmony with Nature: powered by renewables, shaped by decentralized systems, and guided by equity and imagination. Pirate Codes were early models of self-organized societies, built on democracy, fair resource sharing, and mutual aid. Together, they offer a bold blueprint for regenerative, community-led futures. This Fund supports projects, especially from or for island communities, that bring these ideals to life through immersive art, sustainable tech, and playful systems thinking. From solar-powered games to regenerative DAOs, this fund backs techno-optimists designing new systems, by land, sea, and server.

funds.name: SoundEscape Fund for Female Sonic Pioneers
funds.subtitle: Championing independent female music producers who craft original soundscapes with DAWs and push the boundaries of sonic
funds.description: The SoundEscape Fund uplifts women who are reshaping music through intentional sound design. Whether layering real-world textures or composing entirely from scratch, these producers explore new ways to tell stories through sound. This fund supports projects that celebrate experimentation, creativity, and the beauty of building something truly original—one sound at a time.

funds.name: Source Fund for Regenerative Storytelling
funds.subtitle: Supporting under-resourced storytellers whose hopeful, regenerative stories can change how the world thinks, feels, and acts.
funds.description: The stories we repeat become the world we build, and today's dominant narratives are failing us. The Source Fund backs storytellers of every medium, podcasters, filmmakers, writers, comedians, and community voices, whose work is regenerative at heart: hopeful, solutions-driven stories that shift culture rather than feed the doom cycle. The fund is led by Lee Rael, a Cape Town creative director with 25 years in craft and a lifetime in the regenerative movement, and it grows from Source, a social enterprise built for narrative change that intends to reinvest its own profits back into this fund as it grows.

funds.name: SpaghettETH Fund for ETHalian Communities
funds.subtitle: Funding Italy's Ethereum communities to run civic tech projects in their own territories.
funds.description: Italy has quietly grown one of the most populated and positively competitive Ethereum ecosystems in the world: ETHRome, ETHMilan, ETHTurin, ETHVenice, ETHBologna, NapulETH, ETHna, ETHBari. This fund resources those community leads to move beyond events and run local proof-of-concept implementations of Ethereum technology, in partnership with the institutions, universities, and NGOs of their own cities, turning a national community into a network of working public infrastructure.

funds.name: Spark DeSci Fund for Radical Researchers
funds.subtitle: Fueling decentralized science through community-driven research, open collaboration, and transparent innovation.
funds.description: The Spark DeSci Fund supports pioneers building the future of decentralized science. From independent researchers to Web3-native scientific collectives, we champion projects that advance public-good science, open peer review, and interdisciplinary exploration. This fund is a catalyst for scientific innovation and a bridge for new creators to enter the DeSci ecosystem with confidence.

funds.name: Stellar Fund for Financial Empowerment
funds.subtitle: Empowering global innovators to create impactful applications leveraging Stellar's smart contracts and NFTs for a more inclusive financial system.
funds.description: The Stellar Fund is an initiative designed to catalyze projects that harness Stellar's blockchain, with a focus on smart contracts and NFT capabilities. This fund aims to unlock human and economic potential by empowering builders globally to create new digital assets and decentralized financial solutions. The goal is simple yet transformative: enhance cross-border financial inclusion and reshape global finance through groundbreaking projects.

funds.name: Stories Without Borders Fund
funds.subtitle: Empowering underserved Nigerian youth to tell their stories through art & amplify their creative resilience.
funds.description: The Stories Without Borders Fund supports underserved, displaced and marginalized youth in Nigeria, who use art to reclaim their narratives. With a focus on cultural preservation, migration and creative resilience, the fund empowers young creators across photography, sculpting, dance, visual arts and storytelling to transform personal and collective histories into impactful cultural expressions. This is storytelling as survival—and as resistance.

funds.name: Story Fund for Programmable IP
funds.subtitle: Supporting the next wave of applications that harness the power of programmable IP on Story Protocol, the world's first blockchain designed for intellectual property.
funds.description: AI runs on IP—Story makes IP programmable. Story Protocol transforms intellectual property into a liquid, tradable asset, empowering creators to control and monetize their work. The Story Fund for Programmable IP fuels builders who integrate Story’s decentralized IP infrastructure into their applications, pioneering new economic models for AI training, media licensing, and tokenized creative assets. Whether you're building an AI-powered marketplace, on-chain licensing system, or a new IP financial product, this fund supports projects shaping the future of the intelligence economy.

funds.name: Stream of Vectors Fund for Machine Societies
funds.subtitle: For the study of what happens between AI systems, not just between AI and us.
funds.description: As AI systems begin to negotiate, cooperate, deceive, and evolve among themselves, a new field is opening: the study of machine societies. This fund backs researchers, filmmakers, game developers, and writers taking machine-to-machine dynamics as their subject, from emergent communication and AI-versus-AI conflict to drift, confinement, and the stubborn persistence of the human in the loop. Medium-agnostic and subject-specific: a preprint and a playable simulation are equally welcome, and work that crosses between them is especially prized.

funds.name: Tapestry Fund for Decentralized Social Builders
funds.subtitle: Empowering developers to build decentralized, user-owned social apps on Solana.
funds.description: The Tapestry Fund is designed to support projects leveraging Tapestry’s decentralized social protocol to create innovative social applications on Solana. Tapestry offers developers powerful APIs to build onchain profiles, follows, and messaging, ensuring users own and control their social identities across apps. With Tapestry, developers can craft decentralized, scalable social experiences that foster user sovereignty and interoperability. This fund empowers builders to pioneer the next generation of Web3 social apps with fast, secure, and cost-effective infrastructure.

funds.name: Technopenuriaphobia Fund for Human Connection
funds.subtitle: Funding projects that bring people together—offline, in nature—to connect, create, and rediscover what it means to be fu
funds.description: In a world drifting toward screens and simulation, the deepest human magic still happens face to face. Eyes meeting, stories unfolding, and creation emerging in the presence of others and the living earth. Inspired by real-world experiments in community, wilderness journeys, and unplugged gatherings, this Fund supports projects that prioritize embodied connection over digital mediation. From shared rituals to co-created experiences in nature, we back creators building a culture rooted in presence, belonging, and the regenerative power of human connection.

funds.name: Terminus Fund for Network States
funds.subtitle: Supporting sovereign communities that form online, experiment in the real world, and materialize new societies.
funds.description: The Terminus Fund supports sovereign communities and the tools that make them possible. Inspired by the Network State movement and the idea of Terminus as a civilization archive, this fund backs projects that help internet communities pool capital, coordinate action, and materialize shared values—through software, culture, and the direct development of physical territories. From tools and media to monthlong villages and popup cities, we support experiments in collective living that can be shared, forked, and scaled.

funds.name: Test Fund
funds.subtitle: This is a fund
funds.description: asdf

funds.name: The Invisible Illness Fund
funds.subtitle: Supporting creators with invisible illnesses who transform personal pain into public healing through bold, business-savvy creative projects.
funds.description: The Invisible Illness Fund empowers creators living with unseen conditions—like fibromyalgia, Crohn’s, or chronic fatigue—to turn their stories into transformational experiences. Whether through AI, XR, MR, or immersive health innovations, this fund supports those who channel stigma into strength and build projects that educate, heal, and disrupt. We back creators with both the courage to share and the vision to scale.

funds.name: The Sandbox Creator Fund
funds.subtitle: Fueling innovation in The Sandbox metaverse, this fund supports visionary creators building immersive experiences, voxel assets, and groundbreaking content for the ecosystem.
funds.description: The Sandbox Creator Fund empowers artists, designers, and developers to shape the future of the metaverse. Whether you’re crafting interactive experiences, designing voxel-based NFTs, or pioneering new mechanics, we’re here to back your creativity. By funding bold and imaginative projects, we aim to expand the possibilities of The Sandbox, making it a richer, more dynamic world for all.

funds.name: The Weave Fund for Storytellers of the Regenaissance
funds.subtitle: Supporting the storytellers weaving regenerative culture into the fabric of our collective future.
funds.description: The Weave Fund for Storytellers of the Regenaissance supports writers, artists, filmmakers, and multimedia visionaries crafting regenerative stories that seed human and cultural transformation. With a deep commitment to rewilding narratives, amplifying multispecies perspectives, and embodying systemic change, this fund uplifts the storytellers whose work breathes life into regeneration for a thriving planet.

funds.name: Third Place Fund for Community Hubs
funds.subtitle: Supporting builders of modern third places that foster connection, creativity, and collaboration
funds.description: The Third Place Fund backs creators building community hubs that feel like a social club, library, and coffee shop rolled into one. These are physical third places, cosmo-local by design, that offer open access for work, play, and cultural exchange. We fund the next generation of community spaces cultivating deep belonging and global collaboration.

funds.name: tiat fund for creative technologists
funds.subtitle: Fueling Bay Area projects at the intersection of art and technology.
funds.description: The tiat fund supports creative technologists, design engineers, and new media artists in the San Francisco Bay Area. Born from tiat’s grassroots salon series, this fund invests in independent projects that blur the boundaries between code and culture. Whether you're building hardware, software, installations, or experimental experiences, we back the passion projects that define the future of art and tech.

funds.name: Travelling Villages Learning Swarms Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding travelling and pop-up villages where children and families learn together, outside classroom walls, in communities that run on consent.
funds.description: A village does not need a fixed address. Some of the most alive learning environments for children happen in a field for two weeks, in a caravan of families crossing a country, or in a pop-up camp that appears, teaches, and moves on. The Travelling Villages Learning Swarms Fund backs the people building them: travelling and pop-up villages, unschooling groups, wild camps and nature immersions, and family collectives where children follow what they want to learn and the adults take their own growth just as seriously. These are communities that make decisions by consent, treat elders and initiations into adulthood as shared community practice rather than private ceremony, and hold children's culture as part of the village, not an afterthought. Practices vary. Some groups work with Torus Technology, others with Ecovillage Design, others with tools they invented on the road. What they share is a conviction that learning happens wherever a group of people commits to living and growing together. Where the Regenerative Village Culture Fund grows the relational skills inside live-in villages, this fund follows the villages that move, and the children learning inside them.

funds.name: Underbelly Fund for Underground Culture
funds.subtitle: Funding the photographers, filmmakers, zine makers, and organisers documenting and building DIY and underground scenes from the inside.
funds.description: Underground culture is made by people with almost no resources, and it disappears just as fast. A venue closes, a band splits, a collective moves on, a generation gets older, and years of a scene's history go with them. The Underbelly Fund for Underground Culture backs the people best placed to change that: the photographers, filmmakers, zine makers, musicians, archivists, and organisers who are already inside the DIY and underground scenes they document. Born in the punk scenes of Soweto and grown through communities in Kenya, the UK, and Europe, the fund prioritises work that traditional art institutions will not fund and that strengthens a scene while recording it. Every funded project is documented into a shared online archive, so a show in a Johannesburg backyard or a zine run in Nairobi has a permanent home for the people who could not be there. Punk is where it starts. Grassroots culture everywhere is the point.

funds.name: USC ISI Fund for Technological Innovation
funds.subtitle: Fueling groundbreaking research at the intersection of information processing, AI, and cybersecurity.
funds.description: The USC ISI Fund for Technological Innovation is dedicated to empowering researchers to push the boundaries of advanced computing, AI, and information systems. By supporting projects that tackle society's most pressing challenges, this fund champions innovation that redefines what's possible in technology and communication. Whether advancing cybersecurity, exploring quantum computing, or developing AI-driven solutions, this match fund aims to amplify the impact of visionary researchers who are shaping the technologies of tomorrow.

funds.name: Venture Miner Fund for Vibe Coders
funds.subtitle: Empowering the next generation of AI-native builders to safely scale their vibe-coded apps—from weekend hack to world-changing software.
funds.description:
Supporting builders from Zero to One
The Venture Miner Fund supports creators at the bleeding edge of generative AI, turning raw ideas into working software with tools like Replit, Loveable, and Bolt. In this new era, anyone with a spark of curiosity can ship apps with the help of AI—what we call "vibe coding." But code written at the speed of thought needs rails to scale. That’s where Venture Miner steps in. With four years of experience mentoring over 5,000 students in Web3 and AI, we're here to help vibe coders turn their demos into secure, resilient, and scalable products that can stand the test of real-world usage.
Join our community today!
Check out our events calendar and join our community of aspiring vibe coders to receive all the support you'll need for getting started.

funds.name: Village Futures Fund
funds.subtitle: Rebuilding the village for the 21st century, one community at a time.
funds.description: Across the world, people are quietly rebuilding what modern life dissolved: forest schools, rites of passage, regenerative farms, intergenerational gatherings, community arts, and new models of collective care. Most of this work happens in isolation. Village Futures Fund connects and resources these efforts as one movement, supporting creators who are restoring the essential functions of village life and turning them into living models that other communities can learn from and adapt.

funds.name: Voice of the Water Fund
funds.subtitle: For everyone helping water thrive: scientists, artists, communities, and keepers of traditional knowledge.
funds.description: Protecting water takes both science and culture, technology and tradition, action and deep human connection. Voice of the Water Fund supports creators, researchers, conservationists, indigenous leaders, and community organizers dedicated to protecting, restoring, and honoring the waters of our planet: from marine ecosystem monitoring and community-led clean water projects to art that gives rivers and oceans a voice, and practices that deepen the human relationship with water itself.

funds.name: Waste to Wonder Fund for African Creators
funds.subtitle: Supporting African artists, scientists, and innovators turning waste into wonder and climate realities into imaginative, practical solutions.
funds.description: Across Africa, the people living closest to climate injustice, plastic pollution, and biodiversity loss are producing some of the most honest, imaginative, and useful responses on Earth, yet their futures are too often narrated by outsiders while the builders themselves go underfunded. Waste to Wonder Fund exists to change that: backing creators who transform environmental realities into public art, film, fashion, circular products, community science, and digital tools, with a special love for upcycling, the alchemy of turning waste into new, beautiful, useful things. The fund is led by Bethel Clement, a Nigerian conservation biologist and co-founder of UpwardEco, whose work has recovered more than 50 tonnes of plastic waste and helped launch over 40 youth-led sustainability projects, proving that African climate work can be scientifically grounded, culturally powerful, and creatively unforgettable.

funds.name: We’re Loud Fund for DIY Festivals
funds.subtitle: Supporting DIY music festivals organized in unlikely places around the world
funds.description: Inspired by the nomadic spirit of We’re Loud Fest, this Fund backs underground music festivals and events that celebrate human-made sound in unlikely places. We support DIY organizers who bring people together at raw and real events that are much more than just a concert.

funds.name: Weavers Fund for Connected Communities
funds.subtitle: Funding connection: we cover travel costs for bringing communities together
funds.description:
Welcome to the Travelfund for Gathering! This one is for the travelers: researchers, weavers, artists, philosophers, and organizers.
Some of the most important creative work happens when communities meet; and yet little funding exists for the act of gathering itself. Spaces cost money. Travel costs money. The slow work of turning a meeting of minds into a shared tool, a publication, or a new collaboration needs resources. This fund covers those operational costs so that gatherings can happen on purpose, repeatedly, and with direction.
This fund supports open-ended projects built around multiple meetings and a defined mission, not single one-off events: collective of cultural workers building open tools to connect their networks, artist plotting an uprising, or philosophers convening to theorize together and publish what emerges.
Every supported project must commit to an impact outcome.

funds.name: Web3TO Fund for Entrepreneurs
funds.subtitle: Funding the builders of Toronto and Canada's web3 ecosystem.
funds.description: Toronto has one of the most active web3 communities in North America, and Canada's builders deserve backing from inside their own ecosystem. Web3TO Fund supports entrepreneurs and creators doing remarkable things in Toronto and across Canada, with web3 adjacency as the common thread, returning the Web3TO community to its roots: funding great ventures and great people.

funds.name: Wellspring Fund for Water Security
funds.subtitle: Seeking creators of all kinds who secure humanity's access to clean water
funds.description: Water is the quiet dependency under everything we build, and most of the systems around us treat it as an afterthought. Cities send rain to the gutter while aquifers drop; and AI is reshaping society's thirst faster than our infrastructure can answer, drying up rivers that whole cities rely on to survive. The Nurtured Spring Fund for Water Security backs creators who design water into the system from the start: graywater reuse, rain catchment, groundwater restoration, earthworks that turn runoff into native habitat. That work can take the shape of a backyard permaculture garden, an off grid home that is itself a work of art, a community water project, or research that informs how cities and nations manage what is left. The bet is simple: the surest path to water security is thousands of creative people, artists, builders, scientists, and inventors, each finding ways to make sure there is enough, for everyone, for a long time.

funds.name: WildSeed Creators Fund
funds.subtitle: Funding creative, bold ideas from builders and creatives who use creativity to spark imagination and build community
funds.description:
The WildSeed Creators Fund champions artists working at the intersection of public space, technology, and participatory practice. Inspired by the radical legacies of socially engaged art, this fund seeks projects that invite communities to co-create, respond to, and transform their surroundings. Whether IRL or online, we’re looking for creators who treat art as a living, breathing conversation—wild ideas welcome.
The WildSeed Creators Fund champions builders and artists working at the intersections of creativity, technology, and community. Whether your canvas is a city street or oonline, we’re looking for Wild ideas
This fund supports projects that spark imagination at their core. We prioritize projects that integrate technology to foster creativity. From interactive digital installations to large-scale community murals, we want to back projects that provoke imagination and invite people in.

funds.name: Women Who Listen Fund
funds.subtitle: Women creating original music, sound, and immersive audio while building a more connected, collaborative world.
funds.description:
The Women Who Listen Fund supports women who use music as a force for creativity, connection, and cultural change.
The first cohort of this fund serves as a sort of grant program for women musicians specifically for the global majority.
Women from developing countries, countries that have been long colonized, who have less advantage than first world countries are the first to qualify for this fund.
This fund is unique in the sense that it is designed to be a living community that asks members to participate and growth as artists.
Please submit your application here apart from your application through Artizen. It is mandatory to cover all the steps of commitment and joining telegram channel, etc.
https://forms.gle/ncXZbotfQrg2a2UF8
We believe the future of music will be shaped by artists who create together, mentor one another, and build communities that transcend borders and disciplines. From albums and live performances to immersive sound, AI-powered music, educational initiatives, and creative residencies, we champion women whose work expands what's possible through music while inspiring the next generation of creators.

funds.name: Writers Room Fund for AI Storytelling
funds.subtitle: A digital series teaching creators to tell great stories, collaborate, and lead in the age of AI.
funds.description:
The TV writers room has become one of the best creative operating systems of all time.
It was the core creative unit behind the Golden Age of Television—from The Sopranos to Game of Thrones. It taught people how to pitch ideas, take notes, navigate disagreement, develop taste, build creative chemistry, and eventually lead a team.
Now the creative economy is changing. Old career paths are disappearing, new ones are emerging, and millions of storytellers suddenly have access to tools that once required entire studios.
AI will create the biggest explosion of independent storytelling in history.
The Writers Room Fund exists to train, connect, and fund the next generation of storytellers for an economy expanding beyond Hollywood.
That's why our first act is a free digital series: How to Tell Stories in the Age of AI.
We'll take the lessons great writers rooms have always taught—structure, taste, collaboration, creative chemistry, and story leadership—and make them available to everyone, not just the lucky few who get invited into the room.
But we don't just want to talk about The Future of Story. We want to help build it.
As The Writers Room Fund grows, we will also invest directly in a curated portfolio of original projects and host live workshops where writers and creators can develop their craft, find collaborators, and learn how to lead small creative teams.
The digital series lets us reach thousands. The projects let us back promising storytellers. The workshops get people in rooms making things together.
Over time, the strongest ideas from all three can grow into deeper programs, fellowships, and eventually a new kind of creative institution built for the next generation of storytellers.
The old creative map is disappearing. We’re here to discover the next one.
And we believe storytellers should be the ones who lead the way.

funds.name: XR Film Fund for Immersive Storytelling
funds.subtitle: Supporting pioneering filmmakers redefining narrative storytelling through immersive media.
funds.description: The XR Film Fund for Immersive Storytelling champions visionary filmmakers adapting theatrical and cinematic storytelling for immersive media like VR, AR, XR, and MR. We’re seeking scripted fiction projects that fully embrace the narrative and experiential potential of spatial storytelling. From deeply emotional dramas to genre-bending thrillers, this fund supports bold voices exploring the future of cinematic experience.

funds.name: XR Inclusion Fund for African Creators
funds.subtitle: Supporting African XR creators in building a more inclusive, diverse, and representative immersive future.
funds.description: The XR Inclusion Fund for African Creators empowers artists, developers, and storytellers across the continent who are shaping the future of immersive experiences. By providing financial support to underrepresented voices, this fund ensures that African cultures, narratives, and innovations have a lasting impact in the global XR industry. Together, we can create a more equitable and inclusive immersive future.

funds.name: Zanzalu Fund for Future Innovation
funds.subtitle: Seeking builders, artists, technologists, and student founders growing bold ideas out of the Zanzalu community in Zanzibar and East Africa.
funds.description: Zanzalu is a pop-up city on the island of Zanzibar, now in its third year, where local students and creators work alongside founders, artists, researchers, and technologists from around the world. Painter and community organizer Michelle Made grew up on the island watching talented people go unseen for lack of opportunity; through Zanzalu she found her calling connecting them to the wider world, from raising funds to build a computer room for the Straight Center night school to running student weekends on blockchain and technology. This fund is the next step: capital for the projects that sprout from that community, whether a student startup like Zenji Taste that teaches visitors to cook local food, an educator expanding access for kids in underserved neighborhoods, or an artist pushing Swahili futurism onto the global stage. It champions creators with clear vision and deep local roots, and aims to grow into a self-sustaining engine where funded projects give back so the next generation can rise.

funds.name: ZAO Fund for Emerging Culture
funds.subtitle: For the artists and builders of The ZAO
funds.description:
The ZAO Fund for Emerging Culture backs independent musicians, visual artists, technologists, and community organizers building collaborative cultural experiences - where digital coordination meets real-world activation.
We fund projects that use emerging tech (blockchain, AI, immersive systems) not as gimmicks, but as infrastructure for shared ownership, fair pay, and real community. We invest in builders shaping the next wave of culture through collective creation and public engagement, and who collaborate with The ZAO and its community to do it.
